Controller and Registry In Managed Controller mode, TrustedRegistry (registry.yaml) and ControllerConfig (controller.yaml) separate operator-approved execution authority from task requests (see Configuration relationships ). The operator stores registry.yaml (metadata.name) outside any writable repository, pins exact handler and runtime SHA-256 digests, and locks registry.yaml inside controller.yaml by name and SHA-256 (--registry-sha256).
Contents TrustedRegistry ControllerConfig Handlers and profiles Context and MCP bounds Credentials and endpoints Controller controls Recovery TrustedRegistry Store registry.yaml in an operator-owned directory outside cwd, outside dirname(controller.yaml), and outside --repo (otherwise loadTrustedConfiguration refuses with REGISTRY_UNTRUSTED):

update release manifest" Handlers and profiles Handler implementations Each TrustedRegistry.spec.handlers[] entry pins id, version: 1, digest (from installedHandlerDigests()), kind, implementation, parameters, and exact capabilities (<= 256 checkpoints; roles bind resourceIds, resources support conditional when, steps accept handoffs and onRework; see Task Contract ).
Implementation kind Required capabilities Required parameters keys pi.agent.v1 agent ['pi'] prompt (string), purpose ('task' or 'review') pi.compact.v1 agent ['pi', 'compaction'] {} (empty mapping; compacts session context) scope.v1 check ['inert_bytes', 'read_only'] checkId (identifier or null for implicit guard) json-artifact.v1 check ['inert_bytes', 'read_only'] checkId, path, required (key list), equals (scalar map) json-keys-guard.v1 check ['inert_bytes', 'read_only'] checkId, path, allowedPointers (JSON pointer list) line-section-guard.v1 check ['inert_bytes', 'read_only'] checkId, path, startMarker, endMarker no-change.v1 check ['inert_bytes', 'read_only'] checkId (identifier or null for implicit comparison) gate.v1 check ['external_service', 'read_only'] checkId, endpointRef (gateEndpoints[].id), gateId Role and runtime profiles A role profile accepts adapter: pi or adapter: delegated. Secret-free delegated profiles set runtimeRef: null, providerCredentialRef: null, and mcp: null, defaulting context to DEFAULT_DELEGATED_CONTEXT. pi.compact.v1 cannot target delegated roles, and unattended run/resume refuse active or parked delegated roles (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED). ControllerConfig.spec.profiles.roles[] accepts optional selection (provider, model, thinking); --role-model overrides take precedence and persist in run.json.
Top-level TrustedRegistry requires metadata.name (1..64 chars) and spec (version: 1, resourceVersion, handlers, roleProfiles, resources, runtimeProfiles, credentialBindings, environmentBindings; gateEndpoints and publicationEndpoints are optional keys):
Field path Required Values and bounds Meaning roleProfiles[].id Yes Identifier (1..64 chars) Unique role profile ID referenced by ControllerConfig roleProfiles[].selection Yes { provider, model, thinking, api, customProvider? } (off..max; anthropic-messages, openai-completions, openai-responses) Token-based Pi model or custom compatible endpoint; see Model configuration roleProfiles[].tools Yes Subset of read, write, edit, bash, codemode, mcp__workspace__read_file Host-approved tool ceiling for bound task roles roleProfiles[].runtimeRef Yes runtimeProfiles[].id or null for delegated Binds a Pi role to a verified runtime identity roleProfiles[].providerCredentialRef Yes (null allowed) credentialBindings[].id or null Selects the provider credential injected into the broker roleProfiles[].limits No Positive integer map (promptBytes, responseBytes, toolArgsBytes, toolResultBytes, sessionBytes, fileBytes, candidateEntries, toolWallMs, etc.) Optional per-role byte, entry, and tool runtime ceilings runtimeProfiles[].id Yes Identifier (1..64 chars) Unique runtime profile ID runtimeProfiles[].dockerExecutable Yes Absolute path (for example /usr/local/bin/docker) Verified container runtime binary path runtimeProfiles[].dockerSocket Yes Absolute path (for example /var/run/docker.sock) Container runtime UNIX socket path runtimeProfiles[].identity Yes sdkIntegrity, graphDigest (package-lock.json SHA-256), imageDigest (sha256:...), configDigest, profile: 'linux/arm64' Cryptographic runtime lock from describePiAdapterFiles() Context and MCP bounds Context window fields roleProfiles[].context prevents oversized prompts from truncating safety instructions or blowing provider windows:
Field path Required Values and bounds Meaning context.mode No 'proven_bound' (default) or 'estimated_guard' Strict pre-send byte proof vs. estimated window guard context.estimator Yes 'lw-pi-final-json-bytes-v1' Deterministic JSON request byte estimator context.proofId / version / evidence Yes proofId: null, version: 1, evidence: 'estimated' Estimator protocol metadata required by Pi adapter context.workingWindowCeiling Yes Integer 1 .. 16777216 bytes Maximum retained conversation window bytes before compaction context.maxRequestBytes Yes Integer 1 .. 16777216 bytes Maximum single outbound provider HTTP payload size context.serviceMargin Yes Integer >= 32768 bytes Safety buffer reserved for provider system framing context.toolReserve Yes Integer >= 16384 bytes Window space reserved for tool call results context.maxOutputTokens Yes Integer 1 .. 262144 tokens Per-call output token ceiling enforced by the adapter MCP configuration roleProfiles[].mcp (serverId: 'workspace') is required on every roleProfiles[] entry (names: ['mcp__workspace__read_file'], effects: ['read_only'], or [] when unused; idleTimeoutSeconds: 1..2, absoluteTimeoutSeconds: idle..10):
MCP mode Required keys Security constraint Local script mode serverId, scriptDigest, names, effects, idleTimeoutSeconds, absoluteTimeoutSeconds Verifies local MCP helper against localMcpScriptDigest Remote HTTP mode Replaces scriptDigest with transport: 'sessionless-http-json-v1', destinationRef, endpoint, approvedAddresses, credentialRef Requires https://<hostname>/mcp (or http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp) and pinned IP addresses (1..4 IPs) to block DNS rebinding Credentials and endpoints Credential and env bindings Secrets resolve only in memory into a CredentialVault ($$ escapes a literal $), and vault.assertClean aborts if raw secret bytes ever appear in serialized config or state:
Field path Required Values and bounds Meaning credentialBindings[].id Yes Identifier (1..64 chars) Unique credential ID referenced by profiles or endpoints credentialBindings[].consumer Yes 'provider' | 'mcp' | 'gate' | 'publisher' Restricts which subsystem may receive the resolved secret credentialBindings[].destinationRef Yes Identifier (1..64 chars) Target service identifier bound to the credential credentialBindings[].environmentNames Yes Env var list ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) Host environment variables permitted inside template credentialBindings[].template Yes Template string (for example ${LOOPWRIGHT_PROVIDER_TOKEN}) Secret assembly pattern matched identically in ControllerConfig.spec.credentials environmentBindings[].name Yes Env var name ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) Approved host environment variable name environmentBindings[].classification Yes 'credential' or 'nonsecret' Marks whether resolved values are scrubbed as secrets environmentBindings[].paths Yes JSON pointer list (/spec/credentials/<n>/template or /spec/task/...) Exact ControllerConfig paths allowed to reference name Environment interpolation Loopwright expands ${NAME} ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) inside ControllerConfig in a single pass (<= 16 KiB per string) before validating the embedded TaskContract:
Escape and non-execution: Write $$ for a literal $ ($${NAME} stays ${NAME}). Shell command substitution $(...), !command resolvers, and ${NAME:-default} fallbacks never execute (CONFIG_ENV_SYNTAX). JSON Pointer allowlist: Every ${NAME} must match TrustedRegistry.spec.environmentBindings[] at that exact JSON Pointer (CONFIG_ENV_DENIED if unlisted, CONFIG_ENV_MISSING if unset): credential is restricted to /spec/credentials/<n>/template, whereas nonsecret injects non-credential values such as /spec/task/spec/target/sourceRevision. Untrusted manifests: In-repo .loopwright/taskpack.yaml (kind: Taskpack) permits declared non-secret spec.vars ${VAR} interpolation in allowlisted fields, while undeclared or secret ${...} still refuses (TASKPACK_UNTRUSTED_INTERPOLATION), and binds host variables by name via spec.models[].apiKeyEnv. Gate and publication endpoints spec.gateEndpoints and spec.publicationEndpoints are optional top-level keys (0..16 items). Declared items require all keys below (https:// or loopback http://127.0.0.1:<port> / http://[::1]:<port>, no credentials, queries, or #):
Field path Required Bounds Meaning gateEndpoints / publicationEndpoints No 0 .. 16 items (optional keys) Omit when unused; required when gate.v1 or pull_request publication is bound *.id / *.url Conditional Identifier (1..64) / HTTPS URL Required per endpoint item; unique ID and target service URL gateEndpoints[].signingCredentialRef Conditional credentialBindings[].id (consumer: gate) Required per gate item; HMAC key verifying gate.v1 receipts gateEndpoints[].authCredentialRef Conditional credentialBindings[].id or null Required per gate item (null when no bearer header is used) gateEndpoints[].timeoutMs / maxPollMs Conditional 1000 .. 3600000 ms / 1000 .. 3600000 ms Required per gate item; per-request and total polling timeouts gateEndpoints[].pollInitialMs / pollMaxMs Conditional 100 .. 30000 ms / pollInitialMs .. maxPollMs Required per gate item; exponential backoff polling interval bounds gateEndpoints[].jitter Conditional 0 .. 1000 ms Required per gate item; random jitter added between gate polls publicationEndpoints[].signingCredentialRef Conditional credentialBindings[].id (consumer: publisher) Required per publication item; HMAC key verifying PR receipts publicationEndpoints[].authCredentialRef Conditional credentialBindings[].id or null Required per publication item (null when unused) publicationEndpoints[].timeoutMs Conditional 1000 .. 300000 ms Required per publication item; HTTP timeout for PR requests Controller controls Field path Required Bounds and values Meaning spec.task Yes Complete TaskContract object Embedded task contract bound into the run spec.registry.name / digest Yes Registry metadata.name + 64-char SHA-256 Must match registry.yaml bytes and --registry-sha256 CLI flag spec.profiles.roles Yes { roleId, profileRef } (0..16 items) Connects each TaskContract role to a TrustedRegistry RoleProfile spec.profiles.steps Yes { stepId, handlerRef } (0..16 items) Connects each TaskContract step to a TrustedRegistry Handler spec.credentials Yes { ref, template } list (pass [] if none) Declares credential templates interpolated from approved env vars controls.drainReserveMs Yes 5000 .. 600000 ms (< budgets.wallTimeMs) Time reserved before wallTimeMs to drain processes and persist state controls.maxAttempts Yes 1 .. 64 Total execution and repair attempts allowed across the cycle controls.repeatFailureLimit Yes 2 Stops repair loops when the exact same failure signature occurs twice controls.submission Yes mode: 'artifact_or_assistant', path: null or relative path Accepts candidate output from a named workspace file or final assistant turn spec.publication No Defaults to { mode: 'disabled' }; or { mode: 'pull_request', endpointRef, targetBranch, headBranchPrefix, titleTemplate } Optional block; when mode: 'pull_request', all four PR keys are required Recovery Gates and reconciliation Run loopwright check or loopwright run --dry-run before execution. When an external gate or pull request call terminates in unknown, never replay blindly; settle with loopwright reconcile and an authenticated receipt.

Decision Routing System-One decision routing uses fast, calibrated models to classify bounded triage questions (such as capability tier selection, cycle alignment, soft compaction, or candidate diff triage). Routing is strictly advisory: deterministic controller gates and TrustedRegistry rules retain full authority over execution, verification, and publication.
Contents DecisionPolicy Confidence zones Policy reference Live wiring and fallback DecisionPolicy Standalone host policy (decisions.yaml): Load a DecisionPolicy document via loadDecisionPolicyFile('decisions.yaml') in custom controller or App integrations. Declarative Taskpack (spec.decisions): Embed the policy under spec.decisions in .loopwright/taskpack.yaml. Taskpack 2.0 wires spec.decisions live through ControllerPorts.decisions in both GitHub Action and CLI runs. yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: DecisionPolicy spec: enabled: true # Optional in standalone decisions.yaml (defaults to false) disclosurePolicy: public-metadata-only # Optional (defaults to disabled) provider: typesafe-jev # Optional (defaults to typesafe-jev) minConfidence: 0.8 # Optional (defaults to 0.8) confirmThreshold: 0.6 # Optional (defaults to 0.6) hardDeadlineMs: 5000 # Optional (defaults to 5000) maxAttempts: 1 # Optional (defaults to 1) allowImages: false # Optional (defaults to false) For declarative Taskpack triage, declare spec.decisions with optional triageRules:
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: Taskpack metadata: name: docs-sync spec: # Other Taskpack sections omitted; see Taskpack. decisions: enabled: true provider: typesafe-jev # Optional disclosurePolicy: public-metadata-only # Optional minConfidence: 0.8 # Optional confirmThreshold: 0.6 # Optional triageRules: # Optional pre-publication candidate diff rules (0..100) - id: docs-only-risk description: Flag risky config edits outside expected doc files. severity: important kind: noul threshold: 0.7 # Optional finite score in 0.0..1.0 Taskpack nesting: Inside .loopwright/taskpack.yaml (kind: Taskpack), place the spec.* fields under spec.decisions rather than repeating a nested DecisionPolicy header. Threshold order: Validation rejects policies where confirmThreshold > minConfidence (DECISION_POLICY_INVALID). Confidence zones Every calibrated response is routed into one of three deterministic zones based on minConfidence and confirmThreshold:
Zone Confidence range Router action act confidence >= minConfidence Accepts the advisory choice within bounded non-authority scope confirm confirmThreshold <= confidence < minConfidence Requests secondary confirmation or conservative check escalate confidence < confirmThreshold (or timeout/error) Rejects model advice and executes deterministic fallback Policy reference Policy fields In a standalone DecisionPolicy document (decisions.yaml), apiVersion, kind, and spec are required while all spec.* keys default cleanly; when nested under Taskpack spec.decisions, decisions.enabled is required and the shared fields plus triageRules are optional:
Field path Required Default Bounds and meaning apiVersion / kind Conditional — Required in standalone envelope (loopwright.dev/v1alpha1, DecisionPolicy); omit in taskpack.yaml spec.enabled Conditional false Required inside Taskpack spec.decisions; optional in standalone decisions.yaml spec.disclosurePolicy No 'disabled' (standalone) / 'public-metadata-only' (Taskpack) Outbound payload redaction tier (disabled, public-metadata-only, repo-approved-redacted-evidence) spec.provider No 'typesafe-jev' Target provider adapter and wire dialect spec.minConfidence No 0.8 Float in 0.5 .. 1.0; minimum calibrated score required for act spec.confirmThreshold No 0.6 Float in 0.0 .. 1.0 (<= minConfidence); floor for confirm before escalate spec.hardDeadlineMs No 5000 Integer 100 .. 30000 ms shared across all attempts spec.maxAttempts No 1 1 (single call) or 2 (one retry if time remains in hardDeadlineMs) spec.allowImages No false Permits image inputs and box bounding-box questions when true spec.triageRules No Unset Taskpack spec.decisions: 0..100 rules ({ id, description, severity, kind, threshold? }) spec.endpoint / spec.model No Provider default Standalone DecisionPolicy only: custom http(s):// URL and model ID override spec.fallbackRole No null Standalone DecisionPolicy only: fallback role ID or null spec.onFallbackUnavailable No 'blocked' Standalone DecisionPolicy only: 'blocked' or 'deterministic_default' spec.startluxOptions No null Standalone DecisionPolicy only: thinkMode, thinkBudget, gate, allowNone tuning Providers Provider Wire dialect Default model Secret variable typesafe-jev systemone jev-latest TYPESAFE_API_KEY openai-decisions openai-decisions gpt-6-luna OPENAI_API_KEY startlux-decision systemone startlux-decision-27b-autothink STARTLUX_API_KEY microsoft-decision systemone microsoft-decision-1 MICROSOFT_DECISION_API_KEY perplexity-decider systemone pplx-decider-v1.2 PERPLEXITY_API_KEY cloudflare-clef systemone @cf/cloudflare/clef CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN liquid-d1 systemone liquid/d1-ultra LIQUID_API_KEY Disclosure policies Policy Outbound payload ceiling Security rule disabled 0 bytes (no network call) Blocks all outbound provider requests public-metadata-only Redacted metadata (<= 512 chars) Strips raw file contents, diffs, and secrets repo-approved-redacted-evidence Secret-scrubbed evidence (<= 64 KiB) Requires explicit operator approval for repository snippets Question primitives Programmatic @loopwright/decisions callers compose structured requests from four primitives:
Primitive Output shape Constraint choice Single option key (<= 255 options) Supported across all seven providers score Weighted score across 2..10 criteria Supported across all seven providers noul Calibrated binary probability (0.0..1.0) Supported across all seven providers box Normalized bounding box coordinates Requires allowImages: true and vision-capable provider Live wiring and fallback ControllerPorts.decisions exposes the zero-dependency AdvisoryDecisionPort interface so @loopwright/github-app and @loopwright/cli inject live @loopwright/decisions adapters without creating package cycles. Standalone kind: DecisionPolicy defaults disclosurePolicy to disabled, whereas omitting spec.decisions.disclosurePolicy when spec.decisions.enabled: true in kind: Taskpack defaults to public-metadata-only.
Port hook Lifecycle point Safety guarantee routeCapabilityTier Role preparation Preserves pinned role models (userOverridePreserved: true) evaluateCycleAlignment Before repair or rejectTo rework Advisory route (continue, revise, needs_review, blocked) adviseSoftCompaction Prior to pi.compact.v1 steps Cannot veto active hard-compaction triggers triageCandidateDiff Post-capture pre-publication Skips cleanly when triageRules is empty; sets verificationCertified: false Deterministic fallback: Missing provider credentials, timeouts, or unreachable endpoints fall back deterministically (source: 'deterministic_fallback') without blocking or certifying runs. Non-delegable authority: All six DECISION_FORBIDDEN_AUTHORITY_INTENTS (such as certifying verification receipts, bypassing required gates, overriding pinned models, expanding writable scope, or granting execution authority) are permanently refused and never sent to a decision model. Recorded entries appear in run observations (advisoryDecisions) with verificationCertified: false. Sandbox Backends Sandbox policy negotiates OS or container isolation before any agent step runs. When available host backends cannot satisfy your requested capabilities or network policy, negotiation fails closed (SANDBOX_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE or SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_INSUFFICIENT).
Contents Sandbox policy Policy fields Backend choices Network and capabilities Host qualification Sandbox policy Declarative Taskpack mode: Declare spec.sandbox inside .loopwright/taskpack.yaml. The GitHub Action or App negotiates a matching host backend automatically. Managed Controller mode: Pin container/runtime identities in TrustedRegistry.spec.runtimeProfiles[] (see Controller and Registry ) and pass SandboxPolicyInput when invoking native host sandbox wrappers. yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: Taskpack metadata: name: docs-sync spec: # Other Taskpack sections omitted; see Taskpack. sandbox: # Optional host isolation policy preferredBackends: # Optional priority order - macos-seatbelt - linux-bwrap - linux-landlock - docker networkMode: none # Optional (defaults to none) requiredCapabilities: # Optional - filesystemReadContainment - filesystemWriteContainment - protectedPathReadOnlyMask - networkIsolation - processTreeCleanup deniedReadPaths: # Optional extra host paths masked unreadable - ~/.ssh - ~/.aws - ~/.config/gh Priority order: Loopwright probes preferredBackends in order and picks the first backend supporting every listed requiredCapabilities item. Declared policy: Omitting networkMode in an explicit sandbox policy defaults to none. Neutral built-in masks: Locally, sandboxes protect .git and <controlRoot> plus repository-declared scope.protected and deniedReadPaths without hardcoded tool directories. On the GitHub policy profile, .github is also masked read-only unless .github/workflows/** is dual-key unlocked. Read-only bind mounts: Linux bwrap and docker support readOnlyBindMounts for hybrid mountReadOnlyGit (sanitized .git skeleton plus --ro-bind .git/objects), while macOS Seatbelt and Linux Landlock copy .git/objects read-only via single-descriptor 1 MiB streaming. When GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT=github-hosted, and spec.sandbox is omitted, resolveEffectiveTaskpackSandboxPolicy selects direct-dedicated. It sets allow-outbound, requires processTreeCleanup, and enables allowDedicatedDirectOverride. GitHub-hosted runner VMs isolate single jobs, whereas direct execution adds no filesystem or network masks. Self-hosted Actions runners (where RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT is not github-hosted) stay on OS sandbox negotiation.
The turnkey host session supports macos-seatbelt, linux-bwrap, linux-landlock, and direct-dedicated, and blocks docker.
Outside GitHub-hosted Actions runners, an omitted policy selects fail-closed macos-seatbelt, linux-bwrap, or linux-landlock negotiation.
Policy fields spec.sandbox itself is optional inside Taskpack, and every subfield inside spec.sandbox is also optional:
Field path Required Default and bounds Meaning spec.sandbox No Unset Optional sandbox declaration block in Taskpack sandbox.preferredBackends No Host default order (1..5 unique) Ordered candidate backends probed on the execution host sandbox.networkMode No 'none' ('none', 'loopback-only', 'allow-outbound') Socket policy enforced at the OS or container boundary sandbox.requiredCapabilities No Unset (0..6 unique) Isolation guarantees that the chosen backend must provide sandbox.deniedReadPaths No Unset (0..64 entries) Host or ~/-relative paths blocked from read access Backend choices Configure spec.sandbox.preferredBackends[] in priority order:
Backend Isolation mechanism Host prerequisite macos-seatbelt macOS Seatbelt profile (sandbox-exec) Qualified macOS host with /usr/bin/sandbox-exec linux-bwrap Linux namespaces and seccomp (bwrap) Qualified Linux host with /usr/bin/bwrap linux-landlock Linux Landlock LSM rules Linux kernel with Landlock ABI support docker Rootless or daemon container Qualified Docker binary and verified daemon socket direct-dedicated Disposable dedicated runner Actions default for omitted policy; otherwise explicit host opt-in; no filesystem/network masks Network and capabilities Network modes Mode Traffic policy Constraint none Blocks all outbound and loopback sockets Default for an explicit policy without networkMode loopback-only Permits 127.0.0.1 and ::1 traffic only Used for local loopback MCP or runner bridges allow-outbound Permits outbound network connections Actions omitted-policy default or explicit policy opt-in Sandbox capabilities Capability Protection boundary Supporting backends filesystemReadContainment Restricts reads outside workspace and deniedReadPaths Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Landlock, Docker filesystemWriteContainment Restricts writes strictly to candidate writable paths Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Landlock, Docker protectedPathReadOnlyMask Mounts or masks protected paths read-only Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Landlock, Docker networkIsolation Enforces networkMode at kernel or container level Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Landlock, Docker processTreeCleanup Terminates all descendant processes on step exit All five backends syscallFiltering Applies seccomp or container syscall filter profile Bubblewrap and Docker Host qualification Live observations Local fixture checks do not qualify a production host. Before relying on a backend in CI or production, verify the host OS/architecture (darwin/arm64, linux/arm64, linux/x64), installed sandbox binaries, and kernel user-namespace or Landlock support.
Limits and costs Resource limits, timeouts, and token consumption depend on the approved RuntimeProfile and TaskContract.spec.budgets envelope.
See also — Taskpack (embed spec.sandbox in .loopwright/taskpack.yaml) · Controller and Registry (pin runtimeProfiles in registry.yaml)

Task Contract TaskContract defines what bounded work is requested, where files may change, how much time and model budget a run may spend, and which independent checks must pass. In Declarative Taskpack mode, Loopwright compiles TaskContract automatically; in Managed Controller mode, you embed TaskContract inside ControllerConfig (controller.yaml) while keeping credentials and handler digests in TrustedRegistry (see Configuration relationships ).

"packages/app/**" protected: - "packages/app/policy/**" roles: - id: builder adapter: pi provider: zai model: glm-5.3 thinking: high tools: - read - write - edit trustedContext: revision: rev-2026-11 discovery: disabled resources: # Optional pinned context files (use [] when unused) - Mode Admission behavior Controller usage hard_admission Pre-reserves quota in SQLite before dispatch; refuses dispatch if remaining allowance is insufficient Required for wallTime, modelCalls, concurrency, formatRepairs, implementationRepairs, and transportRetries soft_accounting Records actual post-call usage and halts subsequent calls once ceiling is reached Used for tokens because exact output token counts are only known after model generation Acceptance and evidence Artifact manifests An ArtifactManifest uses one of two mutually exclusive spec shapes. Classic { entries } supports up to 256 entries. Admission selects it only if the baseline has at most 128 files and 4 MiB total bytes. Its canonical manifest JSON must fit 32 KiB and its inventory JSON must fit 256 KiB.

ArtifactRef accepts optional uri (<= 2048 chars) and mediaType (<= 128 chars), omitted from canonical serialization when unset. Evidence and EvaluatedCheck accept optional metrics (finite numbers, strings, or booleans), findings, and detail even on passed (Evidence.spec.reason stays null).

Taskpack Taskpack powers Loopwright’s automated mode. Declare repository intent in a bounded YAML document (<= 64 KiB), such as .loopwright/taskpack.yaml or .auto-sync/taskpack.yaml. The host compiles runtime contracts, handler SHA-256 digests, and credential bindings.
For out-of-repo TrustedRegistry governance or CLI controller files, see Task Contract and Controller and Registry .

Under mode: strict, enabling allowHostEnv, allowHostPath, mountReadOnlyGit, allowCheckNetwork, allowAgentNetwork, or command.v1 mountReadOnlyGit: true still needs allow-privileged-execution: 'true' or --allow-privileged. allowWorkflowWrites: true needs allow-workflow-writes: 'true' or --allow-workflow-writes. Multi-tenant webhook runs refuse self-granted privileges (TASKPACK_HOST_BINDING_INVALID / TASKPACK_SCOPE_VIOLATION).
Trust capabilities Field path Strict / privileged Runtime scope execution.mode 'strict' 'strict' or 'privileged'; privileged sets first four capabilities true capabilities.allowHostEnv false / true Inherits host env for preflight and command.v1 while stripping Loopwright/provider/GitHub secrets capabilities.allowHostPath false / true Inherits host PATH for preflight and command.v1 checks capabilities.mountReadOnlyGit false / true Stages sanitized .git skeleton (hooksPath=/dev/null, config stripped) plus --ro-bind or read-only 1 MiB streamed .git/objects for command.v1 capabilities.allowCheckNetwork false / true Grants outbound network for command.v1 checks; avoids nested macOS Seatbelt EPERM when checks run inner sandboxes capabilities.allowWorkflowWrites false / false Dual-key unlock permitting agent edits under .github/workflows/** on GitHub policy profile runs capabilities.allowAgentNetwork false / false Governs resolveEffectiveTaskpackSandboxPolicy / executeSandboxedCommand; turnkey agent-pi bash stays offline-isolated capabilities.allowDockerSocket false / false Requires allow-privileged-execution, allow-docker-socket, and allowCheckNetwork (allow-outbound); binds Docker socket in Linux bwrap digests.pinDigests / lockfile false / <controlRoot>/digests.lock.json Runtime SHA-256 digests freeze runs when false; true enforces lockfile parity via loopwright digest sync spec.vars AST interpolation: Declare 0..64 static non-secret strings ([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*, <= 512 chars). Post-parse single-pass interpolation replaces ${VAR} only in goal.*, publication.titleTemplate/bodyTemplate, roles[].prompt, preflight.env[], and localChecks[].parameters (args[], env, startMarker, endMarker, allowedPointers[]). Undeclared or secret ${...} expressions refuse with TASKPACK_UNTRUSTED_INTERPOLATION. spec.baselineAlignment: Optional { policy: 'off' | 'fail-fast' | 'extract-context', maxConflictFiles, maxConflictBytes } (1..64 default 16; 1024..262144 default 65536). Probes 3-way conflicts in an isolated object store when sourceRevision !== baseRevision. Scope and proposal Field path Required Type and bounds Meaning apiVersion / kind Yes 'loopwright.dev/v1alpha1' / 'Taskpack' Schema version and manifest kind (<= 64 KiB) metadata.name Yes Slug (1..64 chars) Lowercase identifier ([a-z][a-z0-9._-]*) spec.goal.candidate / noChange Yes Strings (1..1024 chars) Role objectives for candidate and no_change runs spec.scope.writable / protected No String lists (1..128 / 0..128) Explicit /** directories, exact files, or single-segment */? globs spec.instructions / skills No Entry or list (1..16 entries) Protected UTF-8 files as paths or { path, when } rules (<= 256 KiB total) spec.target.matrix No null or 1..64 { id, platform, variant } Target matrix metadata passed to TaskContract and memory spec.proposal No { path, requiredFields, schemaVersion } Optional writable .yaml/.yml/.json proposal ledger spec.submission No { path, required? } Optional writable .json agent deliverable path Scope and conditional rules Explicit suffixes: Use dir/** for recursive directories. Paths without /** match exact files or bounded single-segment */? globs (packages/*/package.json), rejecting .. and reserved names. Conditional rules: spec.instructions, spec.skills, and spec.roles[].instructions/skills accept { path, when } predicates (changedPaths, extensions, phases, failedChecks, failureCodes; see Task Contract ). All paths pre-hash at compile time under discovery: 'disabled', enter digests.lock.json and protected paths, and fail with TASKPACK_MANIFEST_INVALID if the same normalized path declares conflicting when predicates. Policy profiles: Under 'local' mode (run --taskpack and step), protection covers .git, <controlRoot> (keeping the spec.proposal.path carve-out), digests.lock.json, manifest scripts, instructions, and skills. Under 'github' mode, .github stays protected and .github/workflows/** requires allowWorkflowWrites. Preflight and upstreams spec.preflight runs once on the host after actor authorization and SecretScrubber initialization (and after spec.triggers enforcement on GitHub entrypoints) and before TaskContract compilation (script must reside under a protected path such as scripts/**, timeoutSeconds 1..3600, explicit env allowlist). It writes JSON to $LOOPWRIGHT_PREFLIGHT_OUT (disposition: 'candidate' | 'no_change' | 'blocked', upstreams[], and stagedResources[]) and may read/write $LOOPWRIGHT_STAGING_DIR.
Staged resources Split mounts: mount: 'prompt' (default for instruction/skill, <= 64 KiB UTF-8, <= 256 KiB total) loads into TaskContract.spec.trustedContext.resources. mount: 'workspace' (default for document, <= 128 MiB per file, <= 256 MiB total) projects read-only files via single-descriptor 1 MiB streaming (O_NOFOLLOW, nlink === 1) into separate workspace and exposeToChecks: true ($LOOPWRIGHT_STAGED_DIR) trees without prompt decoding. Single-link files: Every staged resource must be a single-link (nlink === 1) regular file; pack directories such as npm-cache into a .tgz archive. Upstream kinds Field or value Type or behavior Constraint or default upstreams[].kind 'github-release', 'git-tag', 'git-commit', 'http-json', 'custom-table' watchedPaths (0..64 paths) wired into intake context; allowPrerelease optional versionPath / monotonicSemver Dot/bracket selector and downgrade guard (http-json only) monotonicSemver defaults true; marks downgrades 'held_back' upstreamGroups[] { id, policy: 'lockstep' | 'independent', members: [...] } Under 'lockstep', version mismatch or unavailability marks the whole group 'held_back' atomically 'held_back' status UpstreamAcquisitionStatus value alongside available, up_to_date, blocked, failed Allows sibling available upstreams to proceed while keeping currentVersion in memory Roles and steps spec.roles declares 1..16 roles (id, provider, model, purpose: task | review, thinking, tools: read | write | edit | bash | delete, dependsOn, per-role instructions, skills, handoffs, prompt, mcpServers, models). Review roles default tools to ['read'] and mcpServers to [].
spec.steps declares 1..16 acyclic nodes (id, kind: 'agent' | 'check' | 'compact', role or check, dependsOn, optional handoffs, and optional onRework: { rejectTo, maxReworks } with maxReworks: 1..8). Both spec.roles[].handoffs and spec.steps[].handoffs accept 1..16 StepHandoffSelector entries (fromStep, source, select, maxBytes, required) targeting strict DAG ancestors (see Task Contract ).
Model configuration Model fields spec.models (1..8 items; defaults zai / glm-5.3 / high) accepts token-authenticated Pi HTTP providers and custom baseUrl gateways (allow-custom-base-url: 'true'); interactive OAuth/CLI providers fail closed (PROVIDER_OAUTH_UNSUPPORTED).
Field path Type and bounds Meaning models[].provider / id Slug (1..64) / ID (1..128) Token-based Pi provider or custom provider ID and model identifier models[].thinking / api 'off'..'max' / wire API Reasoning effort and wire dialect (anthropic-messages, openai-completions, openai-responses) models[].apiKeyEnv / baseUrl Env var name / https:// URL Host token env var ([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*) and optional custom gateway URL models[].cost / compat { input, output } / dialect flags Optional USD per million tokens and Pi models.json compatibility options MCP and limits spec.mcp.servers (0..16 items) supports stdio (command, args, env, envFrom, readOnly, timeoutSeconds: 1..600) and http (url, headers, headersFrom, bearerTokenEnv, includeTools). OAuth MCP configs fail closed (MCP_OAUTH_UNSUPPORTED).
Execution limits Action with: inputs override spec.limits, which override LOOPWRIGHT_* env vars. Key bounds: wallTimeSeconds (60..21600), totalTokens (1000..1e9), maxModelCalls (1..1024), maxAttempts (1..16, within 256 checkpoints), commandTimeoutSeconds (1..3600), and limits.overlay: { maxFiles: 1..16384, maxBytes: 1024..17179869184 } (default 128 / 4 MiB, up to 16,384 files and 16 GiB via 1 MiB CAS streaming and single-descriptor staging).
Optional maxTurns and maxRepairTurns (1..1024) cap turns per host-session dispatch; when omitted, defaults derive from compiled maxModelCalls and maxImplementationRepairs. Unlike fallback LOOPWRIGHT_* env vars above, LOOPWRIGHT_MAX_TURNS and LOOPWRIGHT_MAX_REPAIR_TURNS take precedence over spec.limits at runtime.
Verification checks spec.verification.localChecks (0..32 items) and externalGates (0..32 items) evaluate candidate artifacts and scripts inside isolated verifiers.
Local implementations Implementation Key parameters Behavior json-artifact.v1 Scalar expectations (binds spec.proposal) Validates JSON/YAML keys and scalar equality json-keys-guard.v1 path, allowedPointers (/json/pointer) Fails if any JSON key outside allowedPointers changed vs baseline line-section-guard.v1 path, startMarker, endMarker Fails if any line outside delimited marker sections changed vs baseline scope.v1 / no-change.v1 checkId (plus implicit guards) Verifies writable/protected scope or untouched tree parity command.v1 script, args, env, toolchainPaths, mountReadOnlyGit, preserveRepoDirName Mounts the script’s parent directory read-only (whole-tree SHA-256 digest so ./lib.sh works) Command parameters Mounted environment: command.v1 mounts the disposable per-check $LOOPWRIGHT_CANDIDATE_DIR writable (discarded after exit; .git/objects stays --ro-bind when mountReadOnlyGit: true) and keeps $LOOPWRIGHT_BASE_DIR, the script directory, and $LOOPWRIGHT_STAGED_DIR read-only. Existing host directories passed via parameters.env (and safe direct child symlink targets) mount read-only, while /etc, /tmp, repoRoot, runRoot, and $HOME secrets remain denied. Default PATH is /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, so use toolchainPaths only for extra host directories. Structured check output: Writing bounded JSON ({ metrics?, findings?, detail? }, <= 64 KiB; unknown keys such as passed or summary fail closed) to $LOOPWRIGHT_CHECK_OUT propagates through HMAC-signed gate.v1 verdicts (metrics, findings, detail, retryablePreemption) even on exit 0. Inner sandboxes, Docker, and repair early-stop: Checks running inner OS sandboxes should set allowCheckNetwork: true under --allow-privileged. Linux bwrap checks requiring Docker builds must opt into capabilities.allowDockerSocket: true with allow-docker-socket: 'true', allow-privileged-execution: 'true', and allowCheckNetwork: true (networkMode: 'allow-outbound'). Repair prompts instruct agents to submit status: 'blocked' immediately when failures originate in protected check scripts or missing host tools instead of looping until repairNoProgress. externalGates[] support per-gate signingCredentialRef, authCredentialRef, and url. Publication and triggers spec.publication, spec.memory, and spec.triggers are optional in 'local' mode (publication defaults to { mode: 'disabled' }; memory defaults to { directory: '<controlRoot>/memory/default', apply: 'disabled', onNoModelBudget: 'skip' }). GitHub entrypoints enforce spec.triggers before preflight and require PR fields when publication.mode is 'pull_request'.
Field path Type and values Meaning publication.mode / targetBranch 'pull_request' | 'disabled' / branch PR creation or local settlement (optional when disabled) publication.headBranchPrefix / titleTemplate Prefix (1..64) / string (1..256) Managed branch prefix and PR title (optional when disabled) memory.directory / apply <controlRoot>/memory / 'separate-pull-request' | 'local-only' | 'disabled' Protected CAS memory path and mode (ttlDays 15, maxEntries 128, maxPromptEntries 32) memory.onNoModelBudget 'deterministic-observations-only' | 'skip' Behavior without model budget (checkCodeFingerprint, checkUpstreamVersions, publishOnFailure, skipCi) triggers.schedule / workflowDispatch / releasePublished Booleans Permitted GitHub event triggers triggers.commentCommands / commentPrefixes ['retry', 'revise', 'status'] / ['/loopwright'] Authorized PR slash commands and command prefixes spec.sandbox / spec.decisions / spec.output Objects Isolation (Sandbox Backends ), triage (Decision Routing ), and outputs (json, github-step-summary, markdown, text) TaskpackSuite TaskpackSuite (default .loopwright/suite.yaml, <= 64 KiB) coordinates 1..32 domain taskpacks and 0..16 acyclic promotion stages without storing suite state in Git.
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: TaskpackSuite metadata: name: repo-automation spec: domains: - id: docs taskpack: .loopwright/docs.taskpack.yaml enabled: true # Optional schedules: [nightly] # Optional schedule keys stage: stage-a # Optional stage ID matrix: # Optional cell list or scalar map channel: stable - id: runtime taskpack: .loopwright/runtime.taskpack.yaml stage: stage-b # Optional stages: # Optional 0..16 acyclic promotion stages - id: stage-a dependsOn: [] # Optional - id: stage-b dependsOn: [stage-a] readiness: - id: docs-release # Optional kind: github-release source: octocat/engine versionFrom: { domain: docs, path: docs/version.json, jsonPointer: /version } # Optional Suite protection: Action (suite-path) and App (suitePath) domain runs enforce the suite-wide protected union across .loopwright/suite.yaml and peer control paths (<= 128 patterns); gate standalone CLI --taskpack runs with suite check. Branch prefix disjointness: Domains targeting the same targetBranch require pairwise prefix-disjoint spec.publication.headBranchPrefix values (TASKPACK_MANIFEST_INVALID on collision). Stateless readiness: Stage probes (github-release, http-json, git-tag, git-commit) read versionFrom blobs (<= 1 MiB) from baseRevision and defer (eligible / deferred) without Git state files. content:
Architecture Loopwright runs bounded repository work inside isolated sandboxes and verifies every candidate against independent evidence. Choose between simple repository taskpack automation or fine-grained controller and registry governance.
Contents Execution chain Operating modes Configuration surfaces Runtime baseline Trust boundaries Execution chain Admit: Validate task boundaries and acquire a monotonic SQLite lease fence. Execute: Run an isolated Pi role with trusted host bindings and optional decision routing. Verify: Evaluate the candidate against independent checks and authenticated gate receipts. Publish & Remember: Settle pull request publication and propose reviewed memory separately. Operating modes Loopwright supports two distinct configuration and execution modes sharing one verification kernel:
Dimension Declarative taskpack Managed controller Target user Repository maintainers and local CLI users Platform and security operators Files authored One .loopwright/taskpack.yaml in repo Out-of-repo registry.yaml and controller.yaml Digest pinning Compiled automatically by host Pinned manually via SHA-256 (--registry-sha256) Execution graph Single compiled author + check pipeline Custom multi-step agent and check DAG Credential wiring Mapped from local CLI, Action, or App environment Explicit credentialBindings and path templates Key advantage Zero boilerplate; local CLI or GitHub automation Duty separation, custom gates/MCP, local CLI control Walkthrough Declarative Taskpack Managed Controller Configuration surfaces Every Loopwright document uses apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 across declarative and managed configuration surfaces:
Mode or scope Document kind Top-level keys Reference guide Declarative mode Taskpack apiVersion, kind, metadata.name, spec Taskpack Managed mode TrustedRegistry apiVersion, kind, metadata.name, spec Controller and Registry Managed mode ControllerConfig apiVersion, kind, spec Controller and Registry Managed mode TaskContract apiVersion, kind, spec Task Contract Shared policy spec.sandbox Nested under Taskpack.spec Sandbox Backends Shared policy DecisionPolicy apiVersion, kind, spec Decision Routing Entry points Action or GitHubAppConfig Workflow or apiVersion, kind, spec GitHub Action · GitHub App Runtime baseline Deployment host qualification (qualifyDeploymentHostProfile) enforces these baseline prerequisites across Action, App, and CLI surfaces:
Component Baseline requirement Enforcement scope Node runtime Node.js 26.x (built-in node:sqlite) Required across Action, App, CLI, and workspace builds (gpustack/loopwright provisions it automatically) Package manager npm 11.x Workspace dependency installation and builds Host platform darwin/arm64, linux/arm64, linux/x64 Unlisted OS or architecture targets fail closed Storage and clock Local POSIX filesystem; <= 1000 ms clock drift Network mounts (nfs, smb, fuse, sshfs) and clock jumps fail closed Sandbox backend Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Landlock, or Docker Negotiated against taskpack spec.sandbox policy Optional tools Python 3.11+ (runner bridge); Hugo extended 0.152.2+ (docs site) Needed only when exercising runner helpers or building site/ Trust boundaries Trusted hosts bind credentials, runtimes, handlers, and external services. Taskpacks and model output cannot grant authority. Local runs enforce neutral .git and <controlRoot> protection while GitHub entrypoints enforce triggers, PR publication, and .github/workflows/** dual-key locks.
Large overlays stream through SHA-256 verified CAS blob pointers (1 MiB chunks, up to 16,384 files and 16 GiB) instead of inline base64 buffers. Local fixture proof never establishes live provider qualification, and unknown external effects stay unknown until reconciled.

content:
Installation Run Loopwright as a zero-install GitHub Action in target repositories or install the @gpustack/loopwright CLI on a macOS or Linux laptop. After setup, paste a single bootstrap prompt into your coding agent to initialize or migrate repository configuration interactively.
Contents Entry points Prerequisites Step 1: Install CLI Step 2: Verify CLI GitHub Actions Prompt bootstrap Entry points Surface Operating mode Installation method GitHub Action Declarative Taskpack (Simple) Zero local setup; reference uses: gpustack/loopwright@main Host coding agent (loopwright step) Delegated Taskpack or Controller Install @gpustack/loopwright and follow Coding Agents Laptop CLI (npm / pnpm) Managed Controller or local audit npm install -g --ignore-scripts @gpustack/loopwright or pnpm add -g --ignore-scripts @gpustack/loopwright Release tarball Pinned or air-gapped hosts Install gpustack-loopwright-<version>.tgz from GitHub Releases Source checkout Contributors and testers Clone repository, run npm ci && npm run build, and run npm link Prerequisites Local CLI and app-serve hosts must satisfy the runtime baseline : Node.js 26.x (with built-in node:sqlite), npm 11.x, and a local POSIX filesystem on darwin/arm64, linux/arm64, or linux/x64. Provision an approved sandbox backend before executing isolated agent steps.
Step 1: Install CLI npm package Install the single-package CLI globally from npmjs.com using npm or pnpm (--ignore-scripts skips optional transitive lifecycle scripts required by pnpm v10+ build hygiene):
shCopy npm install -g --ignore-scripts @gpustack/loopwright # or with pnpm: pnpm add -g --ignore-scripts @gpustack/loopwright To run one-off commands without a global install, invoke npx or pnpm dlx:
shCopy npx --ignore-scripts @gpustack/loopwright --help # or with pnpm: pnpm --ignore-scripts dlx @gpustack/loopwright --help Release archive Install an immutable release archive directly from GitHub Releases (replace 0.1.0 with the published version):
shCopy npm install -g --ignore-scripts https://github.com/gpustack/loopwright/releases/download/v0.1.0/gpustack-loopwright-0.1.0.tgz Source build Clone the repository to develop locally or test unreleased commits:
shCopy git clone https://github.com/gpustack/loopwright.git cd loopwright npm ci npm run build npm link Step 2: Verify CLI Confirm the binary resolves on your PATH:
shCopy loopwright --version loopwright --help For Managed Controller runs, loopwright init --directory "$HOME/loopwright-ops" writes low-level controller.draft.yaml and registry.draft.yaml skeletons (0600). To initialize a repository .loopwright/taskpack.yaml or migrate existing sync scripts without manual boilerplate, use the interactive bootstrap prompt below.
GitHub Actions Consumer repositories using Declarative Taskpack mode do not need local CLI installation. Add .loopwright/taskpack.yaml and reference gpustack/loopwright@main in .github/workflows/loopwright.yml:
yamlCopy name: loopwright on: workflow_dispatch: {} permissions: contents: read jobs: taskpack: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: gpustack/loopwright@main with: taskpack-path: .loopwright/taskpack.yaml event-name: ${{ github.event_name }} event-path: ${{ github.event_path }} dry-run: 'true' The composite Action provisions Node.js 26 automatically on the runner. Follow GitHub Action for App token wiring and secret bindings.
Prompt bootstrap No custom skill or plugin is required to author Loopwright YAML. Open your coding agent inside the target repository (for example, when migrating an existing automatic synchronized workflow) and paste one prompt:
Taskpack prompt textCopy Read https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/llms.txt and its Bootstrap Interview Reference (https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/references/bootstrap-interview.md). Inspect this repository first WITHOUT editing any files yet, then interview me one question at a time with repository-grounded defaults to agree on which modules to automate or exclude, domain boundaries, update cadence, version/promotion holds, bounded host preflight -> offline sandbox -> independent verifier design, model pool (LOOPWRIGHT_PROVIDER_TOKEN), and workflow panel. Wait for my approval on the design summary before generating Loopwright config (apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1) and running dry-run verification. Controller prompt textCopy Read https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/llms.txt and its Bootstrap Interview Reference (https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/references/bootstrap-interview.md). Inspect this repository first WITHOUT editing any files yet, then interview me one question at a time with repository-grounded defaults to align on writable/protected scope, budgets, verification checks, and role bindings. Wait for my approval on the design summary before computing local Loopwright handler and graph SHA-256 digests, writing out-of-repo registry.yaml and controller.yaml, and validating with loopwright check. See also — Coding Agents (drive zero-secret loopwright step loops from OAuth agents) · Declarative Taskpack (simple automated repository mode) · Managed Controller (fine-grained registry and contract mode)

content:
CLI The CLI validates trusted configuration, syncs taskpack digest lockfiles, and manages bounded local runs. Install the loopwright command on your laptop first via Installation , then use it to prepare, inspect, resume, or reconcile work and audit capability closure.
Contents Step 1: Generate drafts Step 2: Approve bindings Step 3: Check configuration Step 4: Run work Step 5: Inspect recovery Step 6: Audit closure Digest lockfile Delegated stepping Command reference Exit codes Step 1: Generate drafts shCopy loopwright init --directory ./loopwright-config The command creates controller.draft.yaml, registry.draft.yaml, and README.draft.md for Managed Controller workflows (for a complete populated setup, follow Managed Controller ). Note that loopwright init does not generate .loopwright/taskpack.yaml; to bootstrap or migrate a repository Taskpack interactively, use the llms.txt bootstrap prompt .
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: TrustedRegistry metadata: name: operator-draft spec: version: 1 resourceVersion: context-draft handlers: [] roleProfiles: [] runtimeProfiles: [] resources: [] credentialBindings: [] environmentBindings: [] Draft: The excerpt shows the generated registry; controller.draft.yaml contains REVIEW_REQUIRED placeholders that must be replaced before execution. Authority: Keep approved registry bytes and run state outside the checkout. Context: proven_bound is the strict default; estimated guards require explicit immutable opt-in. File Purpose controller.draft.yaml Task, registry name + digest, profile references, and controls registry.draft.yaml Trusted handlers, profiles, resources, and bindings README.draft.md Draft readiness and review instructions Step 2: Approve bindings Review the task scope, exact installed profiles, handlers, credentials, and registry bytes. Replace every placeholder and calculate the SHA-256 of the final approved registry. The generated digest matches only the initial draft bytes.
Step 3: Check configuration shCopy loopwright check --config CONFIG --registry REGISTRY --registry-sha256 DIGEST --json loopwright run --dry-run --config CONFIG --registry REGISTRY --registry-sha256 DIGEST --json loopwright run --dry-run --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml --repo . --json These commands validate and compile statically without running preflight, memory, or publication. Neither proves execution readiness, provider availability, or host qualification. Managed run --dry-run refuses --allow-privileged and --allow-workflow-writes.
Step 4: Run work shCopy loopwright run --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml --repo REPO --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo loopwright run --config CONFIG --registry REGISTRY --registry-sha256 DIGEST --repo REPO --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo loopwright resume --config CONFIG --registry REGISTRY --registry-sha256 DIGEST --repo REPO --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo run --taskpack runs a local declarative taskpack via @loopwright/taskpack without GitHub variables (--taskpack is mutually exclusive with --config/--registry/--registry-sha256). It accepts --mode candidate|no-change|auto, --baseline-alignment off|fail-fast|extract-context, --source-revision <REV>, --role-model, --dry-run, --allow-privileged, --allow-workflow-writes, --json, --output-format, and --step-summary-file.
When --source-revision differs from HEAD, --baseline-alignment probes 3-way merge conflicts in an isolated Git object directory before model calls (fail-fast halts as baseline_merge_conflict, exit 3; extract-context stages scrubbed conflict hunks).
Under local CLI runs without a PR publisher, mode: auto defaults to candidate when neither preflight nor upstreams is declared. Declaring publication.mode: pull_request or memory.apply: separate-pull-request fails closed with TASKPACK_HOST_BINDING_INVALID.
Use resume for an existing run with the same trusted identity and bindings. Do not replay an uncertain external effect.
run, resume, step next, and step submit accept opt-in --allow-privileged (unlocks privileged execution capabilities) and --allow-workflow-writes (unlocks .github/workflows/** writes when the taskpack also enables them). reconcile accepts --allow-workflow-writes and refuses --allow-privileged. Other non-execution commands (init, check, run --dry-run, status, inspect, closure, digest, app-serve) refuse both flags.
run and step runs wire live @loopwright/decisions adapters into ControllerPorts.decisions whenever spec.decisions.enabled is true (falling back deterministically when credentials or endpoints are unavailable).
run, resume, and reconcile accept --output-format <csv> with json, github-step-summary, markdown, and text (each emitting a sanitized Run Health (RunEval) section covering tool repeats, ping-pong loops, repair convergence, per-step/role breakdowns, and autoApplied: false suggestions). Use --step-summary-file <path> to write a separate Markdown summary. With --json, stdout stays pure NDJSON and omits selected Markdown or text reports. Without --json, selected reports go to stdout.
Step 5: Inspect recovery shCopy loopwright status --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo --json loopwright inspect --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo --output INSPECTION_DIR --json loopwright reconcile --config CONFIG --registry REGISTRY --registry-sha256 DIGEST --repo REPO --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo --receipt RECEIPT --json Inspect state and evidence before recovery. loopwright inspect exports run-eval.json inside --output and attaches runEval to JSON output without calling a model or network service. Reconcile an unknown external outcome with its matching authenticated receipt; absent evidence stays unknown.
Step 6: Audit closure shCopy loopwright closure --verify-failures --json Closure exits 0 for a valid report, 3 for falsification or unsupported capability, 4 for failure-matrix failure, and 8 for integrity failure. JSON output uses versioned envelopes with kind, sequence, run identity, and data.
Disposition Evidence scope Meaning closed_local Recorded local evidence level Local criterion and failure matrix passed blocked_external Unprovisioned external dependency Live service, host, or hardware remains external deferred_owned Deferred owned capability Recorded prerequisite remains unimplemented or deferred Digest lockfile shCopy loopwright digest sync --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml --repo . loopwright digest sync --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml --repo . --check --json digest sync computes deterministic SHA-256 digests for spec.preflight.script, mounted command.v1 check directories, instructions, and skills, writing <controlRoot>/digests.lock.json (or spec.execution.digests.lockfile). Pass --check in CI to fail closed (DIGEST_LOCKFILE_DRIFT, exit 4) when any tracked file or check helper drifts.
Delegated stepping Use step to hand each delegated role to a host agent (see Coding Agents for the end-to-end coroutine workflow and overlay application). Start with either trusted configuration or a taskpack:
shCopy loopwright step next --config CONFIG --registry REGISTRY --registry-sha256 DIGEST --repo REPO --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo --json loopwright step next --taskpack TASKPACK --repo REPO --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo --json loopwright step submit --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo --lease TOKEN --status completed --json loopwright step cancel --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo --json Use --action next, --action submit, or --action cancel instead of a positional action. step next accepts --mode candidate|no-change, --baseline-alignment off|fail-fast|extract-context, --source-revision <REV>, --allow-privileged, and --allow-workflow-writes. Pass the same privilege flags to step submit when running command.v1 checks that require privileged host capabilities.
A parked run rejects another pull unless --reissue-lease replaces a lost lease. Submit each single-use --lease token once. --submission-file supplies an artifact; --status accepts completed, no_change, failed, or blocked. Use --reason for a failure or block.
JSON output is NDJSON. An envelope with kind: 'step' contains data.status: 'awaiting_role', selection, prompt, allowed tools, scope, workspace paths, and lease token. Follow those bounds before submitting. Cancellation exits 130; SIGINT and SIGTERM exit 130 and 143, subject to uncertainty precedence.
check, run, resume, and step next accept repeatable --role-model ROLE=PROVIDER/MODEL[:THINKING]. Supply at most eight entries. The CLI limits the argument vector to 64 entries. See Controller and Registry for precedence and persistence.

--output, --json Compile and verify configuration and registry digest statically digest sync --taskpack --repo, --check, --json Write or verify digests.lock.json SHA-256 digests suite check --suite --source-revision, --role-model, --allow-privileged, --allow-workflow-writes, --json, --output-format, --step-summary-file Execute a local taskpack or managed controller run run --dry-run --dry-run with --taskpack+--repo or --config+--registry+--registry-sha256 --mode, --baseline-alignment, --source-revision, --role-model, --output, --json Compile plan statically without preflight, memory, or publication resume --config, --registry, --registry-sha256, --repo, --run-root, --run-id --allow-privileged, --allow-workflow-writes, --json, --output-format, --step-summary-file Resume an existing run under identical trusted bindings step --run-root, --run-id, action --action, --baseline-alignment, --source-revision, --allow-privileged, --allow-workflow-writes, --json Pull, submit, or cancel delegated work status --run-root, --run-id --json Read current run stage, lease state, and checkpoint summary inspect --run-root, --run-id --output, --json Export redacted receipts, run-eval.json, and diagnostics reconcile --config, --registry, --registry-sha256, --repo, --run-root, --run-id, --receipt --output, --json, --output-format, --step-summary-file Settle an unknown external outcome with an authenticated receipt closure None --repo, --output, --verify-failures, --json Audit the 23-capability closure matrix and 14-case failure suite app-serve --config --repo, --json Start the opt-in GitHub App HTTP webhook and token listener Suite commands shCopy loopwright suite check --suite .loopwright/suite.yaml --repo . --verify-digests --json loopwright suite resolve --suite .loopwright/suite.yaml --repo . --event schedule --schedule nightly --json loopwright suite resolve --suite .loopwright/suite.yaml --repo . --event issue_comment --comment-body "/loopwright docs retry" --pr-head-ref loopwright-docs-1 --pr-base-ref main --json suite resolve emits { include: [...] } matrix cells in --json mode and exits 0 for eligible, deferred, and ignored dispositions, 2 for usage, unknown --domain, or manifest/scope validation errors, and 3 for runtime blocked outcomes (such as probe failures or branch-ownership mismatches).
shCopy loopwright app-serve --config github-app.yaml --repo . --json Set spec.listen.enabled: true first. The command exits 2 for disabled or invalid configuration, 130 on SIGINT, and 143 on SIGTERM. See GitHub App for configuration and host requirements.
Exit codes Code Meaning 0 Completed, no change, successful static command, or suite eligible/deferred/ignored 2 Usage, configuration, unknown --domain, or TaskpackSuite manifest rejected 3 Unsupported capability or runtime blocked (baseline_merge_conflict, stage probe, branch mismatch) 4 Execution or acceptance failed 5 Allowance exhausted 6 Deadline expired 7 Reconciliation or ownership needed 8 Authoritative result unavailable or incident 130 Step cancellation or accounted SIGINT, subject to uncertainty precedence 143 Accounted SIGTERM, subject to uncertainty precedence See also — Coding Agents (drive zero-secret loopwright step loops from OAuth coding agents) · Installation (install @gpustack/loopwright and copy bootstrap prompts) · Controller and Registry (approve trusted execution bindings)
