content:
Coding Agents Drive bounded Loopwright runs from OAuth or subscription coding agents without GitHub Actions, GitHub Apps, or provider API keys. Host sessions in Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Cursor, Orca, or Pi pull leased turns via loopwright step.
Install the loopwright CLI first via Installation . Keep --run-root outside --repo and export verified overlays with loopwright inspect before committing local branch changes.
Contents Operating model Skill and prompt Step 1: Pull assignment Step 2: Execute role Step 3: Submit lease Multi-role routing Step 4: Apply overlay Exit codes Operating model Delegated stepping turns Loopwright into a pull-based local coroutine (loopwright step next | submit | cancel). Your host coding agent supplies model execution over its existing OAuth or subscription session, while Loopwright enforces SQLite lease fencing, workspace confinement, and independent check verification.
Zero Loopwright provider credentials, GitHub App keys, or workflow secrets are required on disk or in environment variables. Both operating modes share identical StepYield envelopes and verification gates:
Operating mode Entry flags Role compilation Declarative Taskpack --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml Compiles manifest roles as adapter: delegated with publication.mode: disabled Managed Controller --config, --registry, --registry-sha256 Uses adapter: delegated profiles; set publication.mode: disabled for local-only runs Skill and prompt Portable skill Install the standalone loopwright-step skill into your project or user skill directory:
shCopy npx skills add gpustack/loopwright --skill loopwright-step Or copy .agents/skills/loopwright-step/SKILL.md from a Loopwright checkout into .agents/skills/loopwright-step/SKILL.md (repository scope) or ~/.agents/skills/loopwright-step/SKILL.md (global user scope).
Zero-install prompt When running without local skills installed, paste this prompt into your coding agent inside the target checkout:
textCopy Read https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/llms.txt and fetch https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/latest/docs/operations/coding-agents/index.md. Drive this repository through loopwright step next and loopwright step submit using a disjoint --run-root directory outside the checkout, keep all edits confined to candidateDir, and once result.json settles completed, export a fresh inspect bundle to a new child path and apply candidate.files.json onto my current Git branch. Step 1: Pull assignment Choose a canonical --run-root directory strictly disjoint from --repo (neither inside nor containing --repo, with zero symlink components — resolve pwd -P on macOS where /tmp and /var are symlinks). Start a Declarative Taskpack run:
shCopy RUN_ROOT="$(cd "$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/loopwright-run.XXXXXX")" && pwd -P)" RUN_ID="local-sync-01" loopwright step next \ --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml \ --repo . \ --run-root "$RUN_ROOT" \ --run-id "$RUN_ID" \ --json Host preflight step next --taskpack runs spec.preflight natively without manual staging scripts or --mode auto, and accepts --baseline-alignment and --source-revision. Pass --allow-privileged when the taskpack declares privileged preflight or execution capabilities:
shCopy REPO="$(pwd -P)" loopwright step next \ --taskpack .auto-sync/taskpack.yaml \ --repo "$REPO" \ --run-root "$RUN_ROOT" \ --run-id "$RUN_ID" \ --allow-privileged \ --json Or start a Managed Controller run, pinning target.sourceRevision to git rev-parse HEAD (--mode candidate|no-change is optional):
shCopy loopwright step next \ --config "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" \ --registry "$HOME/loopwright-ops/registry.yaml" \ --registry-sha256 <hex> \ --repo . \ --run-root "$RUN_ROOT" \ --run-id "$RUN_ID" \ --json With --json, stdout emits a versioned NDJSON Envelope ({ version: 1, kind, sequence, runId, data }). When kind is "step", data is a StepYield assignment:
Yield field Type Contract status "awaiting_role" Run is parked at role_pre awaiting external role execution attemptId, stepId string Monotonic attempt identifier and compiled DAG step identifier roleId, purpose string Role identifier and runtime purpose ("task" or "reviewer") repair string Repair turn kind ("none", "format", or "implementation") selection object Resolved { provider, model, thinking } target for role dispatch allowedTools string[] Permitted tool names ([] when repair equals "format") scope object { writable, protected } path rules enforced during capture candidateDir string Staged working tree (<runRoot>/workspaces/<runId>/<attemptId>/candidate) contextFiles string[] Read-only (0o400) context artifacts under .../context prompt string Effective task, review, or format-repair prompt text submissionMode "artifact_or_assistant" Accepts --submission-file or structured --status metadata submissionPath string | null Expected relative artifact path inside candidateDir when configured leaseToken string Single-use 64-character lowercase hex token required on submit Step 2: Execute role Execute the yielded prompt inside candidateDir while obeying every confinement invariant:
Isolated staging: Modify files only inside candidateDir; leave --repo, <runRoot>/<runId>, and <runRoot>/.taskpack-<runId> untouched. Regular files only: Create zero symlinks (O_NOFOLLOW), zero hardlinks (nlink === 1), and zero .git entries inside candidateDir. Overlay bounds: Keep changed or added files within default 128 entries and 4 MiB total (configurable via spec.limits.overlay up to 16,384 files and 16 GiB via 1 MiB CAS streaming; depth <= 32, <= 131,072 scanned entries). Protected invariance: Never modify or chmod 0o400 / 0o500 protected files, .git, <controlRoot>, paths matched by scope.protected, or .github/workflows/** on GitHub policy runs unless explicitly unlocked. Read-only invariance: Leave candidateDir byte-identical when repair === "format" or when allowedTools omits write, edit, delete, and bash (such as purpose: "reviewer"). Step 3: Submit lease Submit the completed role turn with its single-use leaseToken:
shCopy loopwright step submit \ --run-root "$RUN_ROOT" \ --run-id "$RUN_ID" \ --lease "$LEASE_TOKEN" \ --status completed \ --json Pass --submission-file <path> when supplying an external JSON artifact, or set --status (completed, no_change, failed, or blocked) with --reason "<summary>" on non-completed turns. Loopwright captures the overlay, runs independent checks (scope.v1, json-artifact.v1, no-change.v1, and local command.v1 hooks), and emits either the next StepYield (kind: "step") or a terminal result / incident envelope.
Pre-commit scan failures (symlinks, hardlinks, size ceilings, or read-only invariance violations) release authority without consuming leaseToken or deleting candidateDir, so the agent can fix the workspace and re-submit.
Condition Diagnostic code Exit code Duplicate step next while parked OWNER_BUSY 7 Replay or stale leaseToken after rotation AUTHORITY_REFUSED 7 Unattended run or resume on delegated role CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED 3 Recover a lost lease from a crashed worker by rotating the token explicitly (contextFiles reconstruct from CAS for active handoffs), or abort the run cleanly (exit 130):
shCopy loopwright step next --run-root "$RUN_ROOT" --run-id "$RUN_ID" --reissue-lease --json loopwright step cancel --run-root "$RUN_ROOT" --run-id "$RUN_ID" --json Multi-role routing Declare 1 to 4 ordered roles under spec.roles in .loopwright/taskpack.yaml (see Taskpack ) to run multi-agent DAGs such as author-then-reviewer pipelines. During step next --taskpack, Loopwright compiles every role into adapter: delegated automatically; Managed Controller files set adapter: delegated directly on TaskContract.spec.roles[] and TrustedRegistry.spec.roleProfiles[].
Taskpack yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: Taskpack metadata: name: multi-role-sync spec: goal: candidate: Refresh version manifests from upstream releases and pass every local check. noChange: Confirm tracked manifests match upstream releases and settle as no change. scope: writable: - docs - versions.json protected: - policy/invariants.md roles: # Optional — 1..4 roles compiled as adapter delegated during step next - id: author purpose: task provider: anthropic model: claude-sonnet-4-6 thinking: high # Optional tools: # Optional - read - write - edit - bash - id: review purpose: review provider: openai model: gpt-5.4 thinking: high # Optional tools: # Optional - read dependsOn: # Optional - author upstreams: - id: engine kind: github-release source: gpustack/engine watchedPaths: - docs proposal: path: docs/proposal.json requiredFields: - schema_version - summary schemaVersion: 1 verification: localChecks: - id: proposal-json implementation: json-artifact.v1 externalGates: [] publication: mode: pull_request targetBranch: main headBranchPrefix: auto-sync/ titleTemplate: "chore(sync): update upstream manifests" memory: directory: .loopwright/memory/multi-role-sync apply: separate-pull-request onNoModelBudget: deterministic-observations-only triggers: schedule: false workflowDispatch: true releasePublished: false commentCommands: [] Override role models at admission without editing YAML by passing repeatable --role-model <roleId>=<provider>/<model>[:<thinking>] flags (up to 8 unique role IDs, persisted in run.json, total CLI argv <= 64). Dispatch each yielded selection to a matching subagent or supervised Orca worker:
shCopy loopwright step next \ --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml \ --repo . \ --run-root "$RUN_ROOT" \ --run-id "$RUN_ID" \ --role-model author=anthropic/claude-opus-4-6:high \ --role-model review=openai-codex/gpt-5.4:high \ --json Step 4: Apply overlay step next --taskpack sets publication.mode: disabled and pins target.sourceRevision to HEAD’s commit OID automatically. For local-only Managed Controller runs, set publication.mode: disabled and pin target.sourceRevision to git rev-parse HEAD in controller.yaml. Terminal step submit deletes <runRoot>/workspaces/<runId> (candidateDir) while retaining verified artifacts under <runRoot>/<runId>.
Once step submit --json emits kind: "result" with data.result.spec.status === "completed", export the digest-verified bundle to a new --output path (loopwright inspect creates the destination with mode 0700 and rejects pre-existing directories):
shCopy INSPECT_DIR="$(cd "$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/loopwright-inspect.XXXXXX")" && pwd -P)/bundle" loopwright inspect --run-root "$RUN_ROOT" --run-id "$RUN_ID" --output "$INSPECT_DIR" --json Verify $INSPECT_DIR/result.json settled completed, confirm your local Git working tree is clean and HEAD matches the immutable baseline commit OID, and apply $INSPECT_DIR/candidate.files.json onto your branch. candidate.files.json exports version: 2 CAS pointers ({ name, mode, sha256, byteLength, uri, blobPath }, verified via O_NOFOLLOW, nlink === 1, and 1 MiB streaming SHA-256 while preserving 100644/100755 modes), with passive fallback for legacy version: 1 base64 body bundles:
shCopy node -e ' const fs = require("node:fs"), path = require("node:path"), cp = require("node:child_process"), crypto = require("node:crypto"); const [inspectDir, repoArg] = process.argv.slice(1); const repoRoot = fs.realpathSync(repoArg), CHUNK = 1048576; const readJson = (n) => JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(inspectDir, n), "utf8")); const res = readJson("result.json"); if (res.spec?.status !== "completed") throw new Error(`Refusing apply: status=${res.spec?.status}`); const lock = readJson("task.lock.json"), bundle = readJson("candidate.files.json"); if (!lock.spec?.lockHash?.hex || res.spec?.subject?.lockHash?.hex !== lock.spec.lockHash.hex) throw new Error("Refusing apply: lockHash mismatch"); const git = (...a) => cp.execFileSync("git", ["-C", repoRoot, ...a], { encoding: "utf8" }); if (git("status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all").length > 0) throw new Error("Refusing apply: working tree is dirty"); const sourceRev = lock.spec?.contract?.spec?.target?.sourceRevision; if (typeof sourceRev !== "string" || !sourceRev || sourceRev.startsWith("-")) throw new Error("Invalid sourceRevision"); const head = git("rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD^{commit}").trim(); if (head !== git("rev-parse", "--verify", "--end-of-options", `${sourceRev}^{commit}`).trim()) throw new Error("Refusing apply: HEAD != sourceRevision"); const safePath = (rel) => { if (typeof rel !== "string" || !rel || path.isAbsolute(rel) || rel.includes("\\")) throw new Error(`Invalid path: ${rel}`); const parts = rel.split("/"); if (parts.some((p) => !p || p === "." || p === ".." || p === ".git")) throw new Error(`Unsafe segment: ${rel}`); let cur = repoRoot; for (let i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) { cur = path.join(cur, parts[i]); try { const st = fs.lstatSync(cur); const bad = st.isSymbolicLink() || (i < parts.length - 1 ? !st.isDirectory() : (!st.isFile() || st.nlink !== 1)); if (bad) throw new Error(`Unsafe target: ${rel}`); } catch (e) { if (e.code !== "ENOENT") throw e; } } return cur; }; const streamHash = (filePath, expectedLen, outFd) => { const fd = fs.openSync(filePath, fs.constants.O_RDONLY | fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW); try { const st = fs.fstatSync(fd); if (!st.isFile() || st.nlink !== 1) throw new Error(`Unsafe source: ${filePath}`); if (expectedLen !== null && st.size !== expectedLen) throw new Error(`Size mismatch: ${filePath}`); const hash = crypto.createHash("sha256"), buf = Buffer.allocUnsafe(CHUNK); let total = 0, n = 0; while ((n = fs.readSync(fd, buf, 0, CHUNK, null)) > 0) { hash.update(buf.subarray(0, n)); if (outFd !== null) for (let off = 0; off < n;) off += fs.writeSync(outFd, buf, off, n - off); total += n; } const after = fs.fstatSync(fd); if (after.ino !== st.ino || after.dev !== st.dev || after.size !== st.size || after.mtimeMs !== st.mtimeMs) throw new Error(`Source mutated: ${filePath}`); if (expectedLen !== null && total !== expectedLen) throw new Error(`Short read: ${filePath}`); return hash.digest("hex"); } finally { fs.closeSync(fd); } }; const isV2 = bundle.version === 2; if (!isV2 && bundle.version !== 1) throw new Error(`Unsupported bundle version: ${bundle.version}`); const files = bundle.files ?? [], present = new Set(files.map((f) => f.name)); let deleted; if (bundle.manifest?.spec?.baseTree != null) { const commitOid = bundle.manifest.spec.baseTree.commitOid; if (typeof commitOid !== "string" || !/^(?:[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})$/.test(commitOid) || head !== commitOid) { throw new Error("Refusing apply: HEAD != baseTree.commitOid"); } deleted = bundle.manifest.spec.deleted ?? []; } else { if (!/^(?:[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})$/.test(sourceRev) || head !== sourceRev) { throw new Error("Refusing apply: classic snapshot requires pinned commit OID sourceRevision"); } const baseRows = git("ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--full-tree", head).split("\0").filter(Boolean) .map((r) => /^(?:100644|100755) blob ([0-9a-f]{40,64})\t(.+)$/s.exec(r)).filter(Boolean) .map((m) => m[2]); deleted = baseRows.filter((n) => !present.has(n)); } for (const del of deleted) safePath(del); for (const file of files) { safePath(file.name); if (isV2) { if (!/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(file.sha256) || file.uri !== `cas://sha256/${file.sha256}`) throw new Error(`Invalid CAS ref: ${file.name}`); if (!Number.isSafeInteger(file.byteLength) || file.byteLength < 0 || typeof file.blobPath !== "string" || !path.isAbsolute(file.blobPath)) throw new Error(`Invalid blobPath: ${file.name}`); if (file.mode !== "100644" && file.mode !== "100755") throw new Error(`Invalid mode: ${file.name}`); if (streamHash(file.blobPath, file.byteLength, null) !== file.sha256) throw new Error(`Digest mismatch: ${file.name}`); } else if (file.encoding !== "base64" || typeof file.body !== "string") { throw new Error(`Invalid v1 bundle entry: ${file.name}`); } } for (const del of deleted) { const target = safePath(del); fs.rmSync(target, { force: true }); for (let d = path.dirname(target); d !== repoRoot && d.startsWith(repoRoot + path.sep); d = path.dirname(d)) { try { fs.rmdirSync(d); } catch { break; } } } for (const file of files) { const target = safePath(file.name); const v1Bytes = isV2 ? null : Buffer.from(file.body, "base64"); let mode = file.mode === "100755" ? 0o755 : 0o644, unchanged = false; try { const st = fs.lstatSync(target); if (file.mode == null && (st.mode & 0o111)) mode = 0o755; if (isV2) unchanged = st.size === file.byteLength && streamHash(target, file.byteLength, null) === file.sha256 && ((st.mode & 0o111) !== 0) === (mode === 0o755); else unchanged = st.size === v1Bytes.length && fs.readFileSync(target).equals(v1Bytes); } catch {} if (unchanged) continue; fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(target), { recursive: true }); safePath(file.name); const tmp = path.join(path.dirname(target), `.lw-apply-${process.pid}-${Math.random().toString(16).slice(2)}`); const fd = fs.openSync(tmp, fs.constants.O_CREAT | fs.constants.O_EXCL | fs.constants.O_WRONLY | fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW, mode); try { if (isV2) { if (streamHash(file.blobPath, file.byteLength, fd) !== file.sha256) throw new Error(`Digest mismatch: ${file.name}`); } else { fs.writeFileSync(fd, v1Bytes); } fs.fchmodSync(fd, mode); fs.closeSync(fd); fs.renameSync(tmp, target); } catch (e) { try { fs.closeSync(fd); } catch {} fs.rmSync(tmp, { force: true }); throw e; } } ' "$INSPECT_DIR" . Review git status and git diff, run project tests if desired, and commit on your branch.
Exit codes Exit code Outcome 0 step next or step submit yielded awaiting_role, or run settled completed / no_change 2 CLI flag, configuration schema, --run-root overlap, or Taskpack manifest error 3 Run settled blocked, or unsupported capability (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED) 4 Verification check or role execution settled failed 5 Allowance settled exhausted (BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, ATTEMPT_LIMIT, REPEAT_FAILURE) 6 Wall-clock deadline settled expired (DEADLINE) 7 Lease or recovery conflict (OWNER_BUSY, AUTHORITY_REFUSED, RECOVERY_REQUIRED) 8 State, artifact (ARTIFACT_INVALID), limit (OUTPUT_LIMIT), or cleanup incident 130 Run settled cancelled (step cancel or accounted SIGINT) 143 Accounted SIGTERM termination See also — CLI (local operator subcommands and flags) · Taskpack (manifest roles, scope, and checks) · Controller and Registry (delegated role profiles and trusted bindings)

title: Coding Agents

content:
GitHub Action The reusable Action runs a taskpack cycle in a consumer repository without a resident server. It executes optional host preflight, discovers upstream changes, verifies candidates, and can publish a managed pull request.
Contents Workflow Execution and publication Secrets and environment Inputs Outputs Triggers Workflow Install a taskpack and configure the provider and App secrets before enabling this workflow. The App installation needs repository contents and pull request write permissions for native publication.
yamlCopy name: loopwright on: schedule: - cron: '0 3 * * *' workflow_dispatch: {} issue_comment: types: [created] permissions: contents: read jobs: taskpack: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: fetch-depth: 0 persist-credentials: false - uses: gpustack/loopwright@main id: loopwright with: taskpack-path: .loopwright/taskpack.yaml # Optional suite-path: .loopwright/suite.yaml # Optional multi-domain suite domain: docs # Optional suite domain ID resolve-suite-only: 'false' # Optional matrix resolution only baseline-alignment: 'off' # Optional (off, fail-fast, extract-context) mode: auto # Optional (auto, candidate, or no-change) allow-privileged-execution: 'false' # Optional dual-key host unlock allow-workflow-writes: 'false' # Optional dual-key workflow write unlock event-name: ${{ github.event_name }} event-path: ${{ github.event_path }} github-app-id: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_APP_ID }} github-app-private-key: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }} github-app-installation-id: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_APP_INSTALLATION_ID }} # Optional output: json,github-step-summary # Optional env: ZAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_API_KEY }} Mode auto: Runs spec.preflight or upstream discovery, dispatches candidate when updates exist or force is 'true', and compiles a check-only no-change run with zero agent model calls when settled. Suite matrix: Pass suite-path with resolve-suite-only: 'true' to emit outputs.matrix ({ include: [...] }), then run each matrix job with domain: ${{ matrix.domainId }} for per-job revalidation. Comment checkout: Workflows triggered on issue_comment should fetch the PR head commit when running candidate checkout (Suite lookup verifies head.repo.full_name, base.ref, head.ref, and head.sha). Dual-key authority: Even under spec.execution.mode: strict, enabling allowHostEnv, allowHostPath, mountReadOnlyGit, allowCheckNetwork, allowAgentNetwork, or command.v1 mountReadOnlyGit: true requires allow-privileged-execution: 'true'. Enabling allowWorkflowWrites: true independently requires allow-workflow-writes: 'true', and allowDockerSocket: true independently requires allow-docker-socket: 'true' (with allow-privileged-execution: 'true' and allowCheckNetwork: true). Provider: Set the token variable for the selected model, not necessarily ZAI_API_KEY. Runtime: The Action sets up Node.js 26 and builds the workspace if its entrypoint is absent. Execution and publication A live Action enforces policyProfile: github (persisted in run.json), validates spec.triggers strictly before spec.preflight, resolves repository identity and revisions, authorizes the actor, initializes SecretScrubber, runs spec.preflight, and checks for an existing managed PR.
When suite-path is set, intake resolves .loopwright/suite.yaml (verifying PR ownership via GitHub API on issue_comment and refusing cross-fork PRs or domain conflicts), enforces the suite-wide protected union, and revalidates domain eligibility per matrix job before compiling outside the checkout.
Stage Behavior Preflight Validates spec.triggers (and suite-path domain/stage probes) first, then runs spec.preflight.script after actor auth and scrubber setup Align When sourceRevision !== baseRevision, runs isolated 3-way git merge-tree (fail-fast blocks conflicts; extract-context stages scrubbed hunks) before model probes Discover Resolves upstreams, upstreamGroups lockstep holds (held_back), or upstream-records; mode: auto routes no_change to check-only checks Execute Authors a candidate in sandboxed steps with CAS blob pointers and verifies scope and local or external checks; eligible failures can enter bounded repair or rejectTo rework Publish For pull_request mode, consumes shared 3-way merged carry blobs, verifies extracted conflict resolution, and streams verified CAS blobs into a managed PR Pass source-revision when preflight stages writable files onto a commit separate from GITHUB_SHA. Local checks and publication keep protected and non-writable files at GITHUB_SHA, and squash writable changes onto a commit parented on GITHUB_SHA.
Native publication opens each verified CAS blob once (O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW, nlink === 1), streams 1 MiB chunks into git hash-object -w --stdin while verifying SHA-256 and Git blob OID, and commits via a temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE with DCO sign-off and --force-with-lease. It does not embed credentials in remote URLs. An uncertain external outcome remains unknown; do not silently retry it.
Memory finalization follows spec.memory.apply (separate-pull-request, local-only, or disabled) and opens cleanup PRs when stale entries retire. Separate memory PRs skip non-passing runs by default (publishOnFailure: false) and add [skip ci] before the DCO trailer (skipCi: true). Memory errors or skipped updates never block primary task completion.
Local command.v1 checks run through a signed loopback gate against a verified candidate snapshot, mounting the check script’s parent directory read-only with whole-tree SHA-256 verification and exposing $LOOPWRIGHT_BASE_DIR, $LOOPWRIGHT_STAGED_DIR (when exposeToChecks: true), and $LOOPWRIGHT_CHECK_OUT. If a check opts into a GitHub token, grant that token only the permissions the check may use.
On GitHub-hosted Actions runners (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true and RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT=github-hosted), an omitted spec.sandbox selects direct-dedicated. Self-hosted runners negotiate host OS sandboxes instead. The turnkey host session supports macos-seatbelt, linux-bwrap, linux-landlock, and direct-dedicated, and blocks docker. See Sandbox Backends for isolation tradeoffs.
Protected paths override writable paths. .github/workflows/** stays write-protected unless both spec.execution.capabilities.allowWorkflowWrites: true and allow-workflow-writes: 'true' are set. See Taskpack for full manifest fields.
Secrets and environment Pass github-token directly, or pass github-app-id and github-app-private-key to mint an installation token. Explicit github-token takes precedence over App credentials, and App credentials take precedence over ambient GITHUB_TOKEN. When github-app-installation-id is omitted, the Action discovers the repository installation automatically. GH_TOKEN is not the Action token fallback.
The App ID and optional installation ID must be positive integers. The private key is a PEM secret. Restrict installation access to the target repository and required permissions. App tokens can trigger downstream workflows under GitHub’s App event rules.
Credential Purpose github-token or GITHUB_TOKEN GitHub discovery and native PR publication; permissions depend on the operations used. github-app-id, github-app-private-key, github-app-installation-id Mint a repository installation token; installation ID is auto-discovered when omitted. Provider token environment Authenticate live model calls; token variables can contain comma-separated token pools. LOOPWRIGHT_GATE_SIGNING_SECRET Sign external gate requests when a gate endpoint is configured. LOOPWRIGHT_PUBLICATION_SIGNING_SECRET Sign requests to an external publication endpoint. Local command gates and native publication use ephemeral loopback credentials. They do not require external endpoint signing secrets. Generated registry and controller files contain secret references, not raw credentials. Never commit secrets to the repository.
Inputs All Action inputs are optional. Conditional credentials, endpoint bindings, and event payloads depend on the taskpack and trigger.
Input Default Purpose taskpack-path .loopwright/taskpack.yaml Repository-relative manifest path, including a custom control directory. suite-path Unset Optional repository-relative TaskpackSuite manifest path (for example .loopwright/suite.yaml). domain Unset Optional target domain identifier within suite-path. resolve-suite-only false Set true with suite-path to emit outputs.matrix without executing a domain run. baseline-alignment Taskpack off Optional 3-way conflict alignment override (off, fail-fast, or extract-context). mode candidate auto (preflight-driven candidate or check-only no-change), candidate, or no-change. allow-privileged-execution false Dual-key host unlock for spec.execution.mode: privileged or privileged capabilities. allow-workflow-writes false Dual-key host unlock allowing allowWorkflowWrites: true manifests to edit .github/workflows/**. event-name workflow_dispatch GitHub event name; pass github.event_name for other triggers. event-path Unset Event payload path; pass github.event_path for comment and review events. run-root RUNNER_TEMP or ../.loopwright-runs Trusted artifact root outside the checkout. run-id GITHUB_RUN_ID or local Stable run identifier. storage-profile actions-basic Host storage profile: actions-basic or durable. provider, model, thinking Taskpack model pool Override author model selection; thinking levels range from off to max. api, base-url Inferred, unset Wire API and trusted HTTPS endpoint override; base-url requires api. provider-token-env Provider default Environment variable containing a provider token or comma-separated pool. models-json Unset Trusted Pi model configuration path; shell credential resolvers are refused. allow-custom-base-url false Set true to permit model base URLs declared in the taskpack. dry-run false Set true to compile without executing the controller. force false Set true on non-comment triggers to bypass no_change and open-PR deduplication. gate-endpoint-url Unset External gate endpoint, bound as default. publication-endpoint-url Unset External managed publication endpoint; otherwise native PR publication is available. output Taskpack formats or json Comma-separated output formats; overrides spec.output.formats. github-token GITHUB_TOKEN fallback GitHub token for discovery, opted-in checks, and publication; explicit input overrides App auth. github-app-id Unset App ID for installation token minting (overrides ambient GITHUB_TOKEN). github-app-private-key Unset App PEM private key for installation token minting. github-app-installation-id Auto-discovered Optional installation ID; discovered from owner/repo when omitted. git-author-name Dynamic or github-actions[bot] Optional commit author, committer, and DCO Signed-off-by name override. git-author-email Dynamic noreply email Optional commit author, committer, and DCO Signed-off-by email override. upstream-records Unset JSON array of precomputed upstream acquisition records (github-release, git-tag, git-commit, http-json, or custom-table). source-revision GITHUB_SHA Git commit SHA or ref materialized as the candidate source tree while keeping GITHUB_SHA as base revision. mcp-servers Taskpack spec.mcp.servers JSON or YAML MCP server declarations merged by id (LOOPWRIGHT_MCP_SERVERS fallback). wall-time-seconds 3600 Run wall-time limit override in seconds (60..21600; LOOPWRIGHT_WALL_TIME_SECONDS). total-tokens 20000000 Total token ceiling across model calls (1000..1000000000; LOOPWRIGHT_TOTAL_TOKENS). context-window Model catalog or 128000 Model context window token override (1024..10000000; LOOPWRIGHT_CONTEXT_WINDOW). max-output-tokens 32768 Per-call output token ceiling (256..262144; LOOPWRIGHT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS). max-model-calls 256 Maximum model call count per run (1..1024; LOOPWRIGHT_MAX_MODEL_CALLS). max-attempts 5 Maximum controller attempt count (1..16; LOOPWRIGHT_MAX_ATTEMPTS). tool-timeout-seconds 300 Per-tool execution timeout in seconds (1..1800; LOOPWRIGHT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS). command-timeout-seconds 30 Fallback command.v1 check timeout in seconds (1..3600; LOOPWRIGHT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS). Explicit configuration takes precedence over environment variables (Action with: inputs > taskpack.yaml spec.limits > LOOPWRIGHT_* environment variables > compiler defaults). Repair sub-budgets and byte or entry ceilings also accept canonical spec.limits keys and LOOPWRIGHT_* fallbacks; see Taskpack . Interactive OAuth and CLI providers or MCP servers are unsupported.
The force input applies only to candidate discovery on non-comment trigger events (workflow_dispatch, schedule, repository_dispatch, release), while PR comment commands (/auto-sync retry, revise, status) follow comment-command dispatch semantics.
Outputs The Action writes a compact, scrubbed result JSON summary (with SHA-256 digests and byte lengths rather than raw binary buffers) to stdout and GITHUB_OUTPUT. Live runs stream [loopwright] progress lines (upstream discovery, connected MCP servers, per-turn token/duration metrics, tool calls, and check outcomes) plus a plain-text run summary to stderr. A compiled result alone does not establish successful publication; inspect delegateOutcome and the run report.
Output Meaning result Compact structured entrypoint summary and delegateOutcome (ok, detail). pr-url Published PR URL when available; otherwise empty. memory-pr-url Separate memory PR URL when published or updated; otherwise empty. total-tokens Exact integer token subtotal, or 0 when usage is unavailable. cost-usd Six-decimal USD known subtotal when cost provenance is reported or estimated; otherwise omitted. matrix Deterministic JSON matrix ({ include: [...] }) emitted when suite-path resolves. Extended outputs are written for live runs, or for dry runs with an explicit output input. github-step-summary, markdown, text, and json include a sanitized Run Health (RunEval) section with toolRepeats, pingPong, repairConvergence, per-role/per-step breakdowns, and autoApplied: false hints.
Step summaries and human-readable reports format token counts using K/M/B and elapsed durations using ms/s/m/h, while total-tokens and JSON reports preserve exact integers. Estimated cost uses model pricing, not provider-attested billing; missing cost is unknown, not zero.
Format Destination json Structured Action result remains on stdout and GITHUB_OUTPUT. github-step-summary Markdown report appended to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when available. markdown Human-readable report on stderr. text Plain-text report on stderr. totalTokens is the primary usage metric across sinks, with inputTokens and outputTokens breakdowns when available. Human-readable summaries show cost only for reported or estimated provenance. Reports include usage provenance when available. Output is scrubbed and workflow command text is neutralized. Local and fixture tests do not qualify live GitHub publication or provider billing.
Triggers Intake enforces spec.triggers strictly before spec.preflight or execution. Omitted or disabled triggers reject schedule, workflow_dispatch, release, repository_dispatch, and comment events fail-closed. Pass the event name and payload explicitly as shown above; comment commands also require actor authorization.
Install a workflow in each consumer repository. For centralized webhook intake and token brokering, see GitHub App .
See also — GitHub App (configure webhook intake) · Sandbox Backends (select execution isolation)

content:
GitHub App GitHub Action mode is the primary zero-server path for consumer repositories. Use gpustack/loopwright@main for scheduled runs, manual dispatch, and /loopwright comment commands.
The resident HTTP daemon is disabled by default. Operators can opt in for centralized webhook queuing and token brokering; production requires separately qualified ingress and host infrastructure.
Contents App registration Admission and permissions GitHubAppConfig Control plane Host qualification App registration Create a GitHub App in your personal Developer settings or organization settings (https://github.com/organizations/<org>/settings/apps), then install it on the target repositories.
Setting Value Contents Read and write Pull requests Read and write Issues Read and write Metadata Read-only Webhooks Inactive for Action mode; active for app-serve Events For app-serve: Issue comment, Pull request review, Release App secrets Repository or organization secrets: LOOPWRIGHT_APP_ID, LOOPWRIGHT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY Webhook secret LOOPWRIGHT_WEBHOOK_SECRET when app-serve is enabled Use actions/create-github-app-token@v1 with gpustack/loopwright@main in the consumer workflow . The App’s webhook secret and private key must also be available in the trusted daemon environment when enabled.
Admission and permissions Subscribe only to the event types used by your taskpack, including release, issue comment and pull request review as needed. Comment commands are restricted to authorized actors. Verify X-Hub-Signature-256 over raw request bytes with HMAC-SHA256; mismatches and conflicting delivery IDs fail closed. The receiver implements verification before intake.
Installation tokens are restricted to one repository. The read_only profile grants contents and metadata read; publish_pull_request grants contents and pull requests write plus metadata read. Store the App private key and webhook secret in trusted host secret storage.
GitHubAppConfig Save the daemon configuration as github-app.yaml:
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: GitHubAppConfig spec: appId: '12345' webhookSecretEnv: LOOPWRIGHT_WEBHOOK_SECRET privateKeyEnv: LOOPWRIGHT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY apiBaseUrl: https://api.github.com # Optional (defaults to https://api.github.com) listen: # Optional block (set enabled to true for loopwright app-serve) enabled: false # Optional (defaults to false) host: 127.0.0.1 port: 8787 webhookPath: /webhooks/github # Optional (defaults to /webhooks/github) tokenTtlSeconds: 600 # Optional (defaults to 600) maxPayloadBytes: 1048576 # Optional (defaults to 1048576) taskpackPath: .loopwright/taskpack.yaml # Optional repo-relative taskpack path suitePath: .loopwright/suite.yaml # Optional suite path (mutually exclusive with taskpackPath) operatorAllowlist: # Optional GitHub login allowlist for slash commands - release-operator Secrets: Provide environment variable names, not secret values. Listen: Add authenticated ingress before serving external webhooks. Path: taskpackPath and suitePath must be repo-relative, regular files, and mutually exclusive. Field path Required Default Bounds and constraint apiVersion Yes — Must be 'loopwright.dev/v1alpha1' kind Yes — Must be 'GitHubAppConfig' (<= 64 KiB file) spec.appId Yes — Non-empty GitHub App numeric ID or slug (1–64 chars) spec.webhookSecretEnv Yes — Uppercase env var name ([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*) holding HMAC secret spec.privateKeyEnv Yes — Uppercase env var name ([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*) holding App PEM spec.apiBaseUrl No https://api.github.com HTTPS URL (or loopback HTTP); used for tokens and issue_comment PR lookup spec.listen Conditional Unset Optional mapping; required with enabled: true to run app-serve spec.listen.enabled No false Set true to enable loopwright app-serve spec.listen.host Conditional 127.0.0.1 Required when spec.listen is present; keep tenant routes private spec.listen.port Conditional 8787 Required when spec.listen is present; integer 0–65535 spec.listen.webhookPath No /webhooks/github Leading / path; cannot collide with /healthz or /tenants/* spec.tokenTtlSeconds No 600 Integer 60–3600 cached installation token ceiling spec.maxPayloadBytes No 1048576 Integer 1024–26214400 inbound webhook byte cap spec.taskpackPath No Unset Relative regular-file path validated at startup (mutually exclusive with suitePath) spec.suitePath No Unset Relative TaskpackSuite path validated at startup (mutually exclusive with taskpackPath) spec.operatorAllowlist No Unset GitHub login list (1–64 entries) authorized for slash commands Control plane Set spec.listen.enabled: true, bind the named secrets in the trusted environment, then start the daemon:
shCopy loopwright app-serve --config github-app.yaml --repo . The command applies the configured listener and token broker settings. It refuses disabled or invalid configuration. The loader resolves the named webhook secret and private key from the environment.
The service binds loopback by default. Provide authenticated ingress and a configured broker in the trusted host; do not expose tenant lease endpoints publicly. Endpoints include the configured listen.webhookPath (default /webhooks/github), /healthz, and tenant lease and settle routes. The broker issues scoped short-lived tokens and scrubs secrets from responses.
When spec.suitePath is configured, a single verified X-GitHub-Delivery fans out across matching domains while deduplicating redeliveries, enforces the suite-wide protected path union, and binds each leased domain to its per-domain manifest SHA-256 digest. For issue_comment webhooks lacking PR branch metadata, intake queries spec.apiBaseUrl (default https://api.github.com) to verify same-repo PR ownership and target branch routing before admission.
Webhook events Event Trigger surface Admission rule release Published upstream release Enabled via spec.triggers.releasePublished issue_comment Issue or PR /loopwright command Requires collaborator or operatorAllowlist actor pull_request_review Managed PR review comment Requires authorized actor and enabled command schedule Cron workflow run Enabled via spec.triggers.schedule workflow_dispatch Manual operator trigger Enabled via spec.triggers.workflowDispatch repository_dispatch Automation dispatch payload Subject to intake signature and trigger policy Intake dispositions Disposition Queue action Meaning ready Enqueued for tenant Signature, actor, and trigger checks passed no_change Settled without run Upstream discovery found no eligible change blocked Rejected before run Policy, authorization, or payload check refused intake Host qualification Verify the host against the runtime baseline and required sandbox backends before starting app-serve. Interactive MCP OAuth challenges and unsandboxed fallbacks fail closed (MCP_OAUTH_UNSUPPORTED, SANDBOX_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE, SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_INSUFFICIENT).
In-memory queue and delivery state do not establish durable cross-restart recovery.

content:
Declarative Taskpack Declarative taskpack mode is Loopwright’s automated workflow for repository maintainers and local CLI operators. Author one .loopwright/taskpack.yaml file in your repository, and loopwright run --taskpack, loopwright step, or the GitHub Action compiles contracts, handler digests, preflight stages, and credential bindings automatically.
For strict separation between task authors and out-of-repo TrustedRegistry files, or local CLI controller configs, follow Managed Controller instead.
Contents Overview Prompt bootstrap Step 1: Author taskpack Step 2: Validate taskpack Step 3: Configure workflow Step 4: Review outcomes Overview Declarative taskpack mode eliminates manual boilerplate while preserving every Loopwright safety boundary:
Responsibility Authored in taskpack Compiled by Loopwright Work scope Explicit dir/**, exact files, or */? writable and protected paths Adds control paths, scripts, and built-in masks; protected paths win Execution Declare spec.execution, spec.preflight, upstreams, and optional proposal Runs preflight post-auth and compiles TaskContract, ControllerConfig, and TrustedRegistry (0600) Digests Optional digests.pinDigests (digests.lock.json) Computes runtime SHA-256 digests for handlers, check directories, instructions, and skills Secrets Pass GitHub Secrets to Action or App env Generates scoped ${ENV} credential bindings and scrubs preflight and run logs Settlement Choose pull_request or disabled Opens head-pinned PRs or settles check-only no_change runs Prompt bootstrap loopwright init only scaffolds low-level controller drafts; it does not inspect your repository. To run an interview-first setup or migrate an existing automatic synchronized workflow, paste this prompt into your coding agent inside the target repository:
textCopy Read https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/llms.txt and its Bootstrap Interview Reference (https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/references/bootstrap-interview.md). Inspect this repository first WITHOUT editing any files yet, then interview me one question at a time with repository-grounded defaults to agree on which modules to automate or exclude, domain boundaries, update cadence, version/promotion holds, bounded host preflight -> offline sandbox -> independent verifier design, model pool (LOOPWRIGHT_PROVIDER_TOKEN), and workflow panel. Wait for my approval on the design summary before generating Loopwright config (apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1) and running dry-run verification. The agent scans your repository first, interviews you one question at a time with repository-grounded defaults, waits for summary approval, and then writes taskpacks (plus a TaskpackSuite manifest for multi-domain repos), bounded preflight/verifier hooks, and workflows.
Step 1: Author taskpack Create .auto-sync/taskpack.yaml in the target repository. Loopwright derives .auto-sync as the control root.
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: Taskpack metadata: name: docs-sync spec: goal: candidate: Refresh documentation from upstream releases and pass local checks. noChange: Confirm upstream documentation needs no update and settle as no change. execution: # Optional trust mode and lockfile pinning mode: strict # Optional (defaults to strict) digests: pinDigests: true preflight: # Optional post-auth host preflight hook script: scripts/prepare-docs-sync.mjs timeoutSeconds: 120 # Optional scope: # Optional writable: - docs/** protected: - docs/protected-notes.md - scripts/** instructions: # Optional - .auto-sync/prompts/instructions.md upstreams: - id: engine kind: github-release source: octocat/engine watchedPaths: - docs allowPrerelease: false # Optional (defaults to false) proposal: # Optional structured proposal ledger path: docs/proposal.json requiredFields: - schema_version - candidates schemaVersion: 1 verification: localChecks: - id: docs-proposal-json implementation: json-artifact.v1 - id: verify-docs implementation: command.v1 parameters: script: .auto-sync/checks/verify.sh timeoutSeconds: 30 # Optional externalGates: [] # Optional remote gate checks publication: mode: pull_request targetBranch: main headBranchPrefix: loopwright-docs- titleTemplate: "docs - sync upstream documentation" memory: directory: .auto-sync/memory/docs-sync apply: separate-pull-request onNoModelBudget: deterministic-observations-only triggers: schedule: true workflowDispatch: true releasePublished: false commentCommands: - retry - revise - status commentPrefixes: # Optional (defaults to ['/loopwright']) - /loopwright models: # Optional ordered model pool - provider: zai id: glm-5.3 thinking: high # Optional apiKeyEnv: ZAI_API_KEY # Optional - provider: zai-coding-cn # Optional fallback candidate id: glm-5.3 thinking: high # Optional apiKeyEnv: ZAI_CODING_CN_API_KEY # Optional output: # Optional formats: - json - github-step-summary decisions: # Optional live System-One triage policy enabled: true provider: typesafe-jev # Optional disclosurePolicy: public-metadata-only # Optional minConfidence: 0.8 # Optional confirmThreshold: 0.6 # Optional hardDeadlineMs: 5000 # Optional maxAttempts: 1 # Optional allowImages: false # Optional Field dictionary: Inspect every field, bound, and enum in Taskpack . Concise local manifests: Local CLI runs (loopwright run --taskpack and loopwright step) can omit triggers, publication (defaults to disabled), and memory (defaults to disabled). Explicit scopes: Write docs/** for recursive directories and exact paths (or single-segment */? globs) for files. Local runs protect .git and <controlRoot> by default without hardcoded tool directories; declare extra protected paths in scope.protected. Inputs: Create instruction files, preflight.script, and command.v1 scripts under protected paths before running. When configuring spec.proposal.path, place it inside a writable path with a .yaml, .yml, or .json extension. Secrets: Never place tokens or ambient ${ENV} templates inside taskpack.yaml; use spec.vars only for non-secret static values. Delegated role DAG Add roles and optional spec.steps to the taskpack from Step 1. This example runs a read-only review after the author:
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: Taskpack metadata: name: example spec: roles: - id: author provider: example model: author-model - id: review purpose: review provider: example model: review-model tools: [read] dependsOn: [author] Merge these roles into the complete taskpack above; this excerpt omits its other required fields. Run the local delegated loop without Loopwright provider secrets:
shCopy loopwright step next --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml --repo . --run-root ../runs --run-id demo-1 --json loopwright step submit --run-root ../runs --run-id demo-1 --lease TOKEN --status completed --json Work in the yielded candidate directory and obey its allowed tools. Repeat until the run settles. See CLI for leases and Taskpack for role and step bounds.
Step 2: Validate taskpack Verify your host meets the runtime baseline , sync digests.lock.json when pinDigests: true, and validate or execute locally via @loopwright/taskpack before enabling GitHub Actions:
shCopy loopwright digest sync --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml --repo . loopwright digest sync --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml --repo . --check --json loopwright run --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml --repo . --dry-run --json loopwright run --taskpack .loopwright/taskpack.yaml --repo . --run-root ../runs --run-id demo-1 --json Run loopwright run --taskpack ... --dry-run locally or run the GitHub Action with dry-run: 'true' in a pull request workflow to validate the manifest, verify digests.lock.json, negotiate sandbox capabilities, and compile artifacts without invoking preflight, model providers, or branch pushes.
Step 3: Configure workflow Add .github/workflows/loopwright.yml to your repository to run on schedule, workflow_dispatch, or /loopwright issue comments with mode: auto:
yamlCopy name: Loopwright Sync on: schedule: - cron: '0 4 * * *' workflow_dispatch: issue_comment: types: [created] permissions: contents: read jobs: sync: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1 # Optional when minting App PR tokens id: app-token with: app-id: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_APP_ID }} private-key: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }} - uses: gpustack/loopwright@main with: taskpack-path: .auto-sync/taskpack.yaml # Optional custom control root mode: auto # Optional (candidate or check-only no-change via preflight) github-token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }} event-name: ${{ github.event_name }} # Optional (defaults to GITHUB_EVENT_NAME) event-path: ${{ github.event_path }} # Optional for schedule/manual; needed on comments dry-run: 'false' # Optional (defaults to 'false') env: ZAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_API_KEY }} # Optional in dry-run mode LOOPWRIGHT_GATE_SIGNING_SECRET: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_GATE_SIGNING_SECRET }} # Optional when externalGates is empty Action inputs and secrets: Review every input, output, and secret variable in GitHub Action . Centralized webhook server: Deploy a multi-repository intake server via GitHub App . Bootstrap provenance Enforce two provenance rules in comment-driven and self-upgrading workflows:
Trusted checkout: Check out ref: refs/heads/main with persist-credentials: false, pass explicit event-name and event-path, and gate issue_comment jobs to /loopwright pull-request comments from OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR actors. Fetch +refs/pull/<number>/head into .git/objects without checking out unreviewed pull-request heads. Commit SHA pinning: Pin every third-party Action and the bootstrap gpustack/loopwright revision to full 40-character commit SHAs instead of uses: ./ when Loopwright upgrades itself, so candidate branches cannot replace control-plane code or command.v1 verification scripts. Step 4: Review outcomes Reports include total tokens, with input and output breakdowns. Cost appears in human-readable summaries only when reported or estimated.
Candidate pull request: When upstream changes require edits and every check passes, Loopwright opens or updates a head-pinned pull request matching headBranchPrefix. Verified no-change: When preflight or upstream discovery reports no_change under mode: auto, Loopwright runs check-only no-change.v1 verification without invoking agent models. Slash-command iteration: Collaborators with write access comment /loopwright status, /loopwright retry, or /loopwright revise on managed issues or pull requests. Reviewed memory: Active entries live under .loopwright/memory/<name>. Separate PRs skip non-passing runs (publishOnFailure: false) and add [skip ci] (skipCi: true). Use local-only or disabled without blocking task completion. See also — Taskpack (every Taskpack field and enum) · Managed Controller (fine-grained out-of-repo contract and registry workflow)
Next → GitHub Action — configure Action inputs, permissions, and secrets.

Managed Controller Managed controller mode is Loopwright’s fine-grained governance workflow for platform engineers and local CLI operators. You author an out-of-repo TrustedRegistry, pin its SHA-256 digest inside ControllerConfig alongside a TaskContract DAG, and drive admission, execution, inspection, and crash reconciliation via the loopwright CLI.
For single-file repository automation where Loopwright compiles contracts and digests automatically, follow Declarative Taskpack instead.
Contents Configuration relationships Overview Prompt bootstrap Step 1: Generate drafts Step 2: Pin registry Step 3: Author controller Step 4: Execute run Step 5: Reconcile receipts Configuration relationships Managed controller mode coordinates an operator-owned authority store (TrustedRegistry) with a run configuration (ControllerConfig embedding TaskContract):
Relationship Source field Target declaration Runtime invariant Containment ControllerConfig.spec.task Embedded TaskContract (apiVersion, kind, spec) JCS-hashed into run lock; carries zero credentials or handler digests Registry hash lock ControllerConfig.spec.registry.{name,digest} TrustedRegistry.metadata.name + file SHA-256 Must match --registry-sha256 and live outside repo/config roots Role binding spec.profiles.roles[].{roleId,profileRef} Bridges TaskContract.roles[].id to roleProfiles[].id Enforces provider, context ceiling, tool subset, and runtimeRef Step & check binding spec.profiles.steps[].{stepId,handlerRef} Bridges TaskContract.steps[].id to handlers[].id Verifies installed handler SHA-256 and acceptance.checks[].id Context pinning TaskContract.trustedContext.{revision,resources} TrustedRegistry.{resourceVersion,resources[]} Matches context revision and read-only instruction SHA-256 digests Secret & PR wiring spec.credentials[] & publication.endpointRef credentialBindings[], environmentBindings[], publicationEndpoints[] Resolves ${ENV} in memory only; signs HMAC PR/gate requests Overview Prompt bootstrap loopwright init writes generic REVIEW_REQUIRED placeholders. To assemble tailored registry.yaml and controller.yaml files through an interview-first workflow without looking up digests by hand, paste this prompt into your local coding agent:
textCopy Read https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/llms.txt and its Bootstrap Interview Reference (https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/references/bootstrap-interview.md). Inspect this repository first WITHOUT editing any files yet, then interview me one question at a time with repository-grounded defaults to align on writable/protected scope, budgets, verification checks, and role bindings. Wait for my approval on the design summary before computing local Loopwright handler and graph SHA-256 digests, writing out-of-repo registry.yaml and controller.yaml, and validating with loopwright check. Step 1: Generate drafts Install @gpustack/loopwright (see Installation ) and initialize starter YAML files in a real non-symlink directory outside the target repository:
shCopy mkdir -p "$HOME/loopwright-ops" "$HOME/loopwright-runs" "$HOME/loopwright-trust" loopwright init --directory "$HOME/loopwright-ops" cp "$HOME/loopwright-ops/registry.draft.yaml" "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" cp "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.draft.yaml" "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" loopwright init writes 0600 drafts. Keep registry.yaml in $HOME/loopwright-trust outside cwd, outside $HOME/loopwright-ops, and outside any target repository (REGISTRY_UNTRUSTED).
Step 2: Pin registry Compute the installed handler and runtime digests from your Loopwright installation so registry.yaml pins verified code bytes:
shCopy node --input-type=module -e " import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'; import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'; import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'; import { installedHandlerDigests } from '@loopwright/controller'; import { describePiAdapterFiles } from '@loopwright/agent-pi'; const handlers = await installedHandlerDigests(); const pi = await describePiAdapterFiles(); const lock = readFileSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../package-lock.json', import.meta.resolve('@loopwright/agent-pi')))); console.log({ handlers, pi, graphSha256: createHash('sha256').update(lock).digest('hex') }); " Populate $HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml (metadata.name is referenced by controller.yaml):
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: TrustedRegistry metadata: name: prod-operator-registry spec: version: 1 resourceVersion: rev-2026-11 handlers: - id: pi-author version: 1 kind: agent implementation: pi.agent.v1 digest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> parameters: prompt: Update packages/app/manifest.json and satisfy required schema keys. purpose: task capabilities: - pi - id: check-manifest-json version: 1 kind: check implementation: json-artifact.v1 digest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> parameters: checkId: manifest-json path: packages/app/manifest.json required: - schema_version - release equals: schema_version: 1 capabilities: - inert_bytes - read_only - id: scope version: 1 kind: check implementation: scope.v1 digest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> parameters: checkId: null capabilities: - inert_bytes - read_only roleProfiles: - id: builder-profile selection: provider: zai model: glm-5.3 thinking: high api: openai-completions tools: - read - write - edit context: mode: proven_bound estimator: lw-pi-final-json-bytes-v1 proofId: null version: 1 evidence: estimated workingWindowCeiling: 98304 maxRequestBytes: 65536 serviceMargin: 32768 toolReserve: 16384 maxOutputTokens: 1024 runtimeRef: default-runtime providerCredentialRef: zai-token mcp: serverId: workspace scriptDigest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> names: [] effects: [] idleTimeoutSeconds: 2 absoluteTimeoutSeconds: 10 resources: [] runtimeProfiles: - id: default-runtime dockerExecutable: /usr/local/bin/docker dockerSocket: /var/run/docker.sock identity: sdkIntegrity: <sdk-integrity> graphDigest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> imageDigest: sha256:<hash> configDigest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> profile: linux/arm64 credentialBindings: - id: zai-token consumer: provider destinationRef: zai environmentNames: - ZAI_API_KEY template: ${ZAI_API_KEY} environmentBindings: - name: ZAI_API_KEY classification: credential paths: - /spec/credentials/0/template Compute and export the SHA-256 digest of the finalized registry.yaml:
shCopy REGISTRY_SHA=$(shasum -a 256 "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" | awk '{print $1}') echo "$REGISTRY_SHA" Step 3: Author controller Edit $HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml to embed your TaskContract, bind registry.name + $REGISTRY_SHA, and map roles and steps:
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: ControllerConfig spec: registry: name: prod-operator-registry digest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> task: apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: TaskContract spec: goal: Update packages/app/manifest.json release metadata and pass JSON validation. taskpack: app-manifest target: repository: acme/example-app baseRevision: main sourceRevision: v1.4.0 matrix: null scope: writable: - "packages/app/**" protected: - "packages/app/policy/**" roles: - id: builder adapter: pi provider: zai model: glm-5.3 thinking: high tools: - read - write - edit trustedContext: revision: rev-2026-11 discovery: disabled resources: [] budgets: wallTimeMs: 300000 # Must exceed controls.drainReserveMs (120000 ms). totalTokens: 64000 perCallOutputTokens: 1024 maxModelCalls: 8 maxConcurrency: 1 maxFormatRepairs: 1 maxImplementationRepairs: 2 maxTransportRetries: 1 enforcement: wallTime: hard_admission tokens: soft_accounting modelCalls: hard_admission concurrency: hard_admission formatRepairs: hard_admission implementationRepairs: hard_admission transportRetries: hard_admission steps: - id: author-change kind: agent uses: pi-author roleId: builder dependsOn: [] - id: verify-manifest kind: check uses: check-manifest-json roleId: null dependsOn: - author-change acceptance: required: - manifest-json checks: - id: manifest-json allowedEvidenceLevels: - local_execution profiles: roles: - roleId: builder profileRef: builder-profile steps: - stepId: author-change handlerRef: pi-author - stepId: verify-manifest handlerRef: check-manifest-json credentials: - ref: zai-token template: ${ZAI_API_KEY} controls: drainReserveMs: 120000 maxAttempts: 4 repeatFailureLimit: 2 submission: mode: artifact_or_assistant path: null publication: mode: disabled Contract fields: See Task Contract for every TaskContract field and budget invariant. Registry and controller fields: See Controller and Registry for every TrustedRegistry and ControllerConfig field. Step 4: Execute run Run static compilation first (check performs zero network calls and zero state admission), then launch the fenced run outside $HOME/loopwright-trust:
shCopy export ZAI_API_KEY="zai_example_token" loopwright check --config "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" --registry "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" --registry-sha256 "$REGISTRY_SHA" --json loopwright run --config "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" --registry "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" --registry-sha256 "$REGISTRY_SHA" --repo /path/to/example-app --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id run-20261112-01 --json Delegated execution For delegated execution, approve a role profile with adapter: delegated. Set runtimeRef, providerCredentialRef, and mcp to null. Bind the task role to that profile and set its task adapter to delegated. See Controller and Registry for selection and context rules.
shCopy loopwright step next --config "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" --registry "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" --registry-sha256 "$REGISTRY_SHA" --repo /path/to/example-app --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id delegated-1 --role-model builder=example/author-model:medium --json loopwright step submit --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id delegated-1 --lease TOKEN --status completed --json Use the yielded workspace and allowed tools, then submit its single-use lease. Repeat until the run settles. See CLI for recovery and cancellation.
Step 5: Reconcile receipts Query run state, export evidence bundles, or resume/reconcile interrupted executions:
shCopy loopwright status --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id run-20261112-01 --json loopwright inspect --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id run-20261112-01 --output "$HOME/loopwright-runs/bundle-01" Resume after host restart: Run loopwright resume with the same --run-root, --run-id, --config, --registry, --registry-sha256, and --repo. Reconcile uncertain publication (exit 7): Never retry uncertain remote mutations blindly; verify remote state and settle with loopwright reconcile ... --receipt receipt.json (see CLI ). See also — Task Contract (every TaskContract field and budget rule) · Controller and Registry (every TrustedRegistry and ControllerConfig field)

content:
Documentation Loopwright supports two operating modes sharing one verification kernel: Declarative Taskpack (single-file automated repository sync via GitHub Action or App) and Managed Controller (fine-grained out-of-repo TrustedRegistry and TaskContract governance via the CLI).
Getting Started Architecture explains the four-stage execution chain, the two operating modes, and the runtime baseline. Installation installs @gpustack/loopwright, wires GitHub Actions, and provides llms.txt bootstrap prompts. Operations GitHub Action configures the reusable Action and secret bindings in workflows. GitHub App deploys the webhook and token-brokering control plane. CLI runs local compilation, execution, inspection, reconciliation, and closure audits. Coding Agents drives zero-secret delegated loopwright step loops from OAuth coding agents. Walkthroughs Declarative Taskpack walks through simple single-file repository automation and automatic synchronized workflow migration. Managed Controller walks through fine-grained out-of-repo TrustedRegistry, ControllerConfig, and CLI execution. Configuration Taskpack documents every field and enum in .loopwright/taskpack.yaml (Taskpack) and .loopwright/suite.yaml (TaskpackSuite). Task Contract documents every field, budget, step, and evidence tier in TaskContract. Controller and Registry documents every handler, profile, credential, endpoint, and control in TrustedRegistry and ControllerConfig. Sandbox Backends covers native OS and container sandbox policies and capabilities. Decision Routing details System-One advisory confidence zones, providers, and disclosure policies.
